### Content
#### Persona 03 — Brand (Retail and F&B), Individual and Enterprise

---

##### 1. Persona Snapshot

###### Who they are

A **Brand** is a retail chain or a food-and-beverage (F&B) operator looking for stores or outlets. Retail and F&B brands share one role. The brand's own asset class (Retail or F&B) is fixed at sign-up.

| | Individual Brand | Enterprise Brand |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **How they join** | Self-serve: phone number, one-time code, one short form | Set up offline by the Keydemand team (usually after the free limit, a website enquiry, or sales outreach) |
| **Who logs in** | One person | Several people, each with their own mobile number |
| **Demands** | 3 free in total, then an Enterprise pitch | Unlimited |
| **Contact reveals** | 5 free, then an Enterprise pitch | Unlimited |
| **Saved formats and sub-brands** | Not available | Available. The brand picks "Post for" a sub-brand or the umbrella brand |
| **Relationship Manager** | None | A dedicated Keydemand manager, shown on the profile |
| **WhatsApp and email** | On (can be switched off) | Always off. In-app and push only |
| **Deactivate or delete own account** | Yes | Not allowed. Contact the Relationship Manager |

###### Goals

- Post what space the brand needs, once, and get matched properties and projects.
- Reach the right broker or landlord quickly.
- Keep sensitive requirements away from competing brokers where Keydemand takes them over.

###### What a Brand can and cannot do

| Can | Cannot |
| :---- | :---- |
| Post demands in **its own asset class** (Retail brand posts Retail, F&B brand posts F&B) | Post properties |
| Explore properties in Retail, F&B **and Office** | Explore Managed Space properties |
| Browse and show interest in projects | Browse other people's demands (Keydemand staff only) |
| Reveal supplier phone numbers (5 free) | Buy an agent subscription (agents only) |
| Request hidden photos from owners | Open the Leads page (Keydemand staff only) |
| Approve or decline contact requests on its own demands | Change its asset class after sign-up |
| Save properties and projects | Choose who can see its demand (fixed: agents and Keydemand) |

###### Limits and paywalls at a glance

| Limit | Individual | Enterprise |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Demands | 3 for the whole brand, for life. The first one is posted at sign-up | Unlimited |
| Contact reveals | 5 for life | Unlimited (counter not used) |
| What happens at the limit | A full-screen prompt to explore Enterprise Solution | Not applicable |

###### Asset-class scope

| Action | Retail brand | F&B brand |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Post a demand** | Retail only | F&B only |
| **Explore properties and projects** | Retail, F&B, Office | Retail, F&B, Office |
| **Cannot see** | Managed Space | Managed Space |

---

##### 2. Screen and Navigation Map

###### Where the menu items appear

| Surface | Items shown to a Brand |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Desktop top bar** | Explore Properties, Post Demand, Enterprise Solution |
| **Desktop profile menu** | Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager (enterprise only), Saved, Notifications |
| **Phone drawer** | Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager (enterprise only), Saved, Notifications, Explore Properties, Post Demand, Enterprise Solution |
| **Phone bottom bar** | Home, Explore, Dashboard, Menu |
| **Menu tab (mobile app)** | Explore properties, Projects, Saved, Post Demand, Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager, Notifications, Enterprise Solution, About Us, Our Clients, Investors, Contact Us, FAQs, Privacy, Terms, Cookie Policy |

**Never shown to a Brand:** Post Property, Explore Demands, Subscription, Leads, Agent Subscription, List Project (guests only).

###### Screens

| Screen | Purpose | Gate |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Home | City-based feed: featured projects, new properties, exclusive projects, developer projects | Public |
| Search / Explore | Properties and projects with filters | Public (photos hidden when signed out) |
| Property detail | Full listing, contact reveal, request photos, PDF, save | Public (limited) |
| Project detail | Brochure, units, Show Interest, PDF, save | Public (limited) |
| Post Demand | The shared requirement form | Signed in. Blocked by the limit prompt when the free demands are used |
| Demand detail | Own demand, matches, edit, deactivate, delete, PDF, share link | Owner (or account team for enterprise) |
| Dashboard | Overview, Demands, Leads, Enquiries tabs | Signed in |
| Saved | Saved properties and projects | Signed in |
| Notifications | Notification centre | Signed in |
| Profile and Edit Profile | Details, notification switches, deactivate, delete | Signed in |
| Enterprise Solution | Enquiry form | Public. **Hidden inside the iPhone app** |
| Delete Account | Deletion request form | Signed in |
| Contact, FAQs, About, Our Clients, Investor Relations, Privacy, Terms, Cookie settings | Information pages | Public. FAQs hidden inside the iPhone app |

###### Mobile versus desktop

- The profile is a full page on desktop and a drawer entry on phones.
- The iPhone app hides every sales message (Enterprise Solution, FAQs, upgrade buttons). A limit prompt shows the limit only, with a Close button.
- Push notifications exist only in the mobile apps. The Profile page shows the push switch only there.

---

##### 3. End-to-End Flows

###### Flow 1 — Sign up as a new Brand

- **Actor:** A new brand representative.
- **Prerequisites:** An Indian mobile number that can receive SMS. Nobody has registered with it before.

**Steps**

1. Open **Sign in** ("Welcome aboard"). Enter the 10-digit mobile number. Tick the box accepting the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.
2. **Continue** stays grey until both are done. Pressing it anyway explains why: "Enter your mobile number." / "Enter a valid 10-digit number." / "Please accept the Terms of Use & Privacy Policy to continue."
3. The system finds no account. The **Choose your role** screen appears with four cards: Property Agent, Retail Brand, F&B Brand, and Office / Managed Space Tenant.
4. Pick **Retail Brand** or **F&B Brand**. The card lists the free benefits: post a demand, contact up to 5 brokers, shortlist, relevancy results.
5. A six-digit code is sent by SMS. Enter it. The code submits itself when you enter the sixth digit. Pasting works.
6. The **Post your space requirement** form opens (see the field table below). Fill every starred field.
7. Tick the consent box and submit. If a required field is empty, a pop-up lists exactly which ones.
8. The system checks the chosen location **before** creating the account. If it is in another city, the pop-up "Check the location" says: "[Place] is in [City], outside [Selected city]. Pick a location inside [Selected city]." Nothing is created yet.
9. The account and the first demand are created together. The brand lands on the **You're in!** screen: "Your requirement has been posted. Our team will match you with verified properties." The button reads **See matches for your requirement**.

**Registration form fields (Brand)**

| Field | Required | Notes |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |
| Brand Name | Yes | Shown on the demand if the brand chooses to show its name |
| Your Name | Yes | Contact person |
| Official Email ID | Yes | Checked for format, disposable domains and a working mail server |
| Transaction Type | Yes | Lease or Buy |
| City | Yes | Picked from the served cities |
| Location / Area | Yes | Picked from a map search. Must sit inside the city |
| Carpet Area (sq. ft.) | Yes | One number. The system stores it as a range with the same minimum and maximum |
| Other nearby localities | No | Up to three extra localities in the same city |
| Store Type | Yes | One choice: Highstreet or Mall |
| Floor Preference | Yes | Ground or Any |
| Possession Needed | Yes | Immediate, Within 3, 6 or 9 months, After 9 months |
| Terms consent | Yes | Required to continue |

**System side-effects**

- A **company** and **brand** record are created behind the scenes. The brand is marked Individual and tied to Retail or F&B.
- If the brand name already exists, a toast appears: "Your brand name matches a brand already on Keydemand — our team will verify your brand details shortly." The account still works.
- WhatsApp updates and all notification types start switched on.
- The first demand is posted to **Agents and Keydemand team**. It uses up **one of the three free demands**.
- A **Welcome** message goes out (in-app, WhatsApp, email).
- If the user leaves after the code but before the form, a **Profile incomplete** WhatsApp reminder goes out 24 hours later, and the number is remembered as a half-finished sign-up.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | What the user sees |
| :---- | :---- |
| Wrong code | "That OTP is incorrect. Check the code and try again." |
| Old code | "Your code expired. Tap Resend for a new one." |
| Too many wrong codes | "Too many attempts. Request a new code." |
| Asking for a code too soon | "Please wait N seconds before requesting another OTP." The button counts down |
| Many requests | "Too many OTP requests. Try again in N seconds." |
| Registration session expired | "Your registration session has expired. Start again." |
| Number already registered | "An account with this mobile number already exists. Sign in instead." |
| Account created but demand failed | Green screen, then a yellow note: "Your account is ready, but your requirement was not saved. Post it again to start getting matches." Button: **Post your requirement** |
| Resuming an abandoned sign-up | The brand is asked to choose Retail or F&B again, because only "Brand" was remembered |
| Enterprise brand tries to self-register | Not allowed. The brand is told to use Enterprise Solution |

---

###### Flow 2 — Sign in (returning Brand)

- **Actor:** An existing brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** An active account.
1. Enter the mobile number and accept the consent tick. Continue.
2. A six-digit code arrives. Enter it.
3. The user lands on the page they came from, or on Home.
4. Sessions refresh quietly. After a long idle period the user is asked to sign in again: "Your session has expired. Please sign in again."

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Brand switched off by Keydemand | "This brand account has been deactivated. Contact Keydemand for help." (the brand's own users are refused until Keydemand restores the brand) |
| User deactivated it themselves | A pop-up offers **Reactivate account** or **Not now** |
| Keydemand deactivated the account | A pop-up asks the user to contact support |
| Account deleted | "This account has been removed. Contact support." |

---

###### Flow 3 — Post a demand (the full form)

- **Actor:** A brand user (individual, or enterprise team member).
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. Free demands remain (individual), or the brand is enterprise.

**Steps**

1. Open **Post Demand**. The system first checks the free allowance. If it is used, the limit prompt appears instead of the form (Flow 4).
2. The page shows a progress meter and these sections. The asset class is **locked** to the brand's own class.
3. Fill the **Primary Details**, **Additional Details**, **Amenities** and (for lease) **Transaction** sections.
4. Optional: save a draft. Leaving with unsaved changes asks "Save your draft before you go?". A returning user sees "Draft restored" with **Discard draft** and **Dismiss**.
5. Press **Post Retail Demand** or **Post F&B Demand**. A pop-up lists any missing required fields.
6. A confirmation toast says the requirement is live. The demand opens in the dashboard.

**Field groups by asset class**

| Group | Retail (lease) | Retail (buy) | F&B (lease) | F&B (buy) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Format (enterprise only)** | Sub-brand pick | Same | Same | Same |
| **Primary Details** | Transaction type, City, Location, Other interested locations (up to 3), Map link (optional), Carpet area, Possession needed, OC required | Same, plus **Budget** | Same as Retail lease | Same as Retail buy |
| **Additional Details** | Ceiling height (ft), Frontage (ft), Store type, Floor preference, Show my name, Extra notes (optional) | Same | Same | Same |
| **Amenities** | Fit-outs required, Washroom required, plus the amenity picker. Brand lease form leaves out Parking and Mezzanine | Fit-outs, Washroom, Parking, Mezzanine, amenities | Fit-outs, Washroom, Parking, Non-veg served, Cooking type (Electric, Gas, Either), kitchen amenities | Same as F&B lease |
| **Transaction** | Lease tenure (years), Lock-in (years) | Not shown | Lease tenure, Lock-in | Not shown |
| **Documents** | Not shown | Required documents: Floor Plan, Autocad, Fire NOC, Other Licenses | Not shown | Required documents (same four) |

**Rules on the form**

- **Required:** Transaction type, City, Location (picked from the map list), Carpet area, Possession needed, Store type, Floor preference. For lease, the lock-in cannot be longer than the lease tenure: "Lock-in cannot be more than the lease tenure of N years."
- **Show my name on this demand:** Off by default. The form shows the live preview "Posted by [Brand name]" or, when off, "Posted by Retail Brand" / "Posted by F&B Brand". The brand name must exist in the profile to be used.
- **Amenities:** Retail and F&B share one amenity list. The picker shows how many are selected.
- **Audience:** A Brand cannot pick who sees the demand. It is always shown to **agents and the Keydemand team**. Any attempt to change it is ignored.
- **Demand card picture:** The brand's logo if one is uploaded. Otherwise a stock picture for the asset class.

**System side-effects**

- One free demand slot is used (individual brands).
- The demand is checked for **high-value routing** (Flow 15).
- A **Requirement posted** receipt appears (in-app, not counted in any daily cap).
- **Production:** the demand waits for Keydemand approval before it is live and matched. Test environments approve automatically.
- Matching starts as soon as the demand is live (Flow 16).

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Brand tries the other asset class | "Your account cannot post this type of demand." |
| Buy and managed space | Not applicable to brands |
| Draft exists | Offered back on the next visit |
| Duplicate or conflicting values | The form shows each problem beside its field, all at once |
| Format picked by an individual brand | Prompt: "Formats are an Enterprise feature" |

---

###### Flow 4 — Hit the free demand limit and the Enterprise pitch

- **Actor:** An individual brand with three demands used.
- **Prerequisites:** Free allowance used up.
1. The brand opens **Post Demand**. The page does not open. A prompt stands in front.
2. The prompt says the account includes three free demands and pitches unlimited postings, priority matching with landlords and a dedicated Relationship Manager.
3. Buttons: **Explore Enterprise Solution** and **Back to Dashboard**.
4. If the brand tries through another route, the server refuses: "Free brand limit (3 demands) reached. Upgrade to Enterprise to post more."
5. An in-app message also appears: "You have used all 3 requirements on your plan. Enroll for Enterprise Solution to post more." with an **Enroll** button.

**Rules**

- The count belongs to the **brand**, so every user under the brand shares it.
- It never goes back down. Deleting a demand does not return a free slot. The delete screen says so.
- Enterprise brands skip this check.
- Inside the iPhone app the prompt shows the limit only. There is no upgrade button.

---

###### Flow 5 — Enquire for Enterprise Solution

- **Actor:** Any visitor or brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** None. Not available in the iPhone app.
1. Open **Enterprise Solution** from the menu or from the limit prompt.
2. Fill: Full Name (required), Company (required), Work Email (optional, checked if given), WhatsApp Number (required, +91 fixed), Primary City Focus, Brand Type (Retail, F&B, Office or Managed Space).
3. Press **Submit Enquiry**. A **Thank you for your enquiry** panel replaces the form, with **Submit another enquiry**.
4. Errors: "Couldn't submit your enquiry — please try again."

**System side-effects**

- A sales lead is recorded as "New". If the visitor is signed in, the lead links to their account.
- It appears in the Control Panel Enquiries list. A Keydemand member follows up offline.
- No account change happens automatically.

---

###### Flow 6 — Becoming an Enterprise Brand (offline)

- **Actor:** The Keydemand team, then the brand.
- **Prerequisites:** An enquiry (Flow 5), a direct request, or sales outreach.
1. Keydemand and the brand agree terms offline. Requirements and brand parameters are collected outside the app.
2. A Keydemand admin creates or upgrades the account, sets up the brand page, sub-brands and saved **Formats** (size, frontage, floor, fit-out), adds each team member's mobile number, and assigns a Relationship Manager. Details: Control Panel guide.
3. Each team member signs in with their own number and code.
4. The brand sees: unlimited demands, the **Post for** sub-brand picker, a **Team demands** view, a Relationship Manager card, and locked-off WhatsApp and email.

**What changes for the brand**

| Area | Before | After |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Demands | 3 free | Unlimited |
| Contact reveals | 5 free | Unlimited |
| Demand form | Plain | Format picker. Asset class and constant fields can be pre-filled |
| Who can manage demands | The poster | **Every user of the brand** can read, edit, deactivate and delete all the brand's demands |
| Help | Contact page | Relationship Manager card, plus **Ask my RM** on each demand |
| WhatsApp and email | Optional | Off and locked |
| Deactivate or delete | Self-service | Only through Keydemand |

---

###### Flow 7 — Explore properties and projects

- **Actor:** A brand user, or a visitor.
- **Prerequisites:** None. Signed-in users see photos.
1. Open **Explore Properties** from the menu or bottom bar. The page opens on the saved city and the brand's own class.
2. Switch between **Property** and **Projects**. A **Demands** option does not appear.
3. Use filters. Sort by Most Recent, Price: Low to High, Price: High to Low, or Area: Largest First.
4. Turning on **Office** for the first time shows a notice that it is outside the brand's own category. The notice is asked once per visit.
5. Open a card for the full detail page.

**Filter groups**

| Group | Options |
| :---- | :---- |
| Listing type | Property, Projects |
| Transaction | Lease, Sale |
| Asset class | Retail, F&B, Office (Managed Space is not offered) |
| Store type | Highstreet, Mall |
| Floor | Floor choices (ground, upper floors and bands) |
| Availability | Immediate, within 3, 6, 9 months |
| Fit-out | Furnished, unfurnished and similar |
| Amenities | The shared amenity list |
| Facilities | Washroom, parking, signage allowed |
| Legal | OC status |
| Ranges | Area and price ranges |
| Projects only | Project status, project type, Mixed Use, seats, total project size |

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Brand asks for a class it may not see | The request is narrowed silently to the allowed classes |
| Signed out | Photos hidden. Contact reveal asks the visitor to sign in first |
| Listing limited to certain audiences | Brand sees it only if one of the ticked groups describes it (for example Retail brand or Enterprise brand) |
| Cities | Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Pune and Hyderabad appear in the quick filters. The full served list is in the city picker |

---

###### Flow 8 — View a supplier's phone number (contact reveal)

- **Actor:** A brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. The listing is live and visible to the brand.
1. On a property or demand card or detail page, tap **View number**.
2. If signed out, the user is sent to sign in, then returned and the reveal continues.
3. The system checks, in order: already revealed (free, shown again), own listing, listing still live, audience allows the brand, then the allowance.
4. **Property or ordinary demand:** the number reveals at once in a **Contact Unlocked** pop-up with the contact's name, the number, a **Copy** button and a **Call [first name]** button.
5. A free reveal is counted.
6. After five free reveals the prompt appears: "Brand accounts include 5 free contact views. Go Enterprise to reveal unlimited supplier numbers, with priority matching and a dedicated relationship manager."

**System side-effects**

- A record of the reveal is saved with its source (free, subscription, owner, approved or Keydemand).
- The owner is told someone viewed their number, as an in-app "Someone viewed your contact" row and a line in the 6 pm summary.
- An enterprise brand is never counted.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Listing deactivated, deleted or not approved | "This listing is no longer available." |
| Own listing | "This is your own listing." |
| Listing hidden from the brand's group | "Property not found" |
| Free views used | The Enterprise prompt (individual) |
| Request closed because the listing ended | The free reveal is **given back** |

---

###### Flow 9 — Request hidden photos

- **Actor:** A brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. The owner marked some photos hidden.
1. On the property page, hidden photos show a **Request images** button.
2. A confirmation pop-up says **Image Request Sent** with "Awaiting owner approval". Button: **Got it**.
3. The owner is alerted (in-app, push, WhatsApp) with **Share images**.
4. **Approved:** the brand gets "Images are now available for [ID]" and sees all photos from then on.
5. **Declined:** "Your image request for [ID] was not approved." The request is closed.
6. No answer in 72 hours: the request expires.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| A second request for the same listing | "You have already sent a request for this listing." |
| Own listing | "You cannot send a request on your own listing." |
| Listing ended first | The request closes and the brand is told "Your request was closed because the property is no longer available." |

---

###### Flow 10 — Brand as recipient: approve or decline a contact request

- **Actor:** Brand user (any user of the brand for enterprise).
- **Prerequisites:** An agent or Keydemand member asked for the number on the brand's demand.

**Why this exists:** A demand posted by a brand is the one case where reveal needs approval. Every other number reveals at once.

1. The requester taps **View number** on the brand's demand. A request is created instead of a reveal. They see "Request sent — the owner will approve. Track it under Enquiries."
2. The brand is alerted (in-app, push, WhatsApp; individual brands only) with **Approve or decline**.
3. Open **Dashboard → Leads → Contact requests**. Each row shows the requester type, the demand and a **New** badge.
4. Press **Accept**: "Request approved — your number is now visible to them."
5. Or press **Reject**, confirm "Reject this request?", then "Request rejected".
6. The requester is told the result. Approved: "Contact request approved, tap to view the number." Declined: "Contact request not approved."
7. If the brand does nothing for **72 hours**, the request expires. The requester sees it as unanswered.

**System side-effects**

- Accepting writes the reveal record. The requester can now see the brand contact.
- A request already answered cannot be changed: "This request has already been actioned."
- If the demand ends before an answer, the row shows an "unavailable" label without Accept or Reject.

**Keydemand-held brand demands**

When Keydemand posts a demand on a brand's behalf, the demand **reads as the brand**. Nobody asks the brand to approve. The revealed phone is the Keydemand member's, shown under the brand's name (or "Retail brand" or "F&B brand" if the brand hides its name). Every active user of the brand is told of each reveal and enquiry, and the acting person is never told about their own action.

---

###### Flow 11 — Leads and "numbers viewed"

- **Actor:** A brand user.
1. Open **Dashboard → Leads**.
2. **Contact requests** lists people asking for the brand's number, with the open ones flagged.
3. **Phone numbers viewed** lists people who unlocked the brand's number. Tapping a person shows their history.
4. The Leads card on the Overview shows an alert when a contact request is waiting.

Brands do **not** see an Image requests inbox, because brands do not post properties.

---

###### Flow 12 — Dashboard

- **Actor:** A brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. Brands see four tabs: **Overview, Demands, Leads, Enquiries**. There is no Properties tab.

| Tab | What it shows |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Overview** | Counts for Demands, Leads and Enquiries. Each opens its own tab. A short list of relevant properties and projects |
| **Demands** | The brand's demand cards, filterable by asset class. Each card shows matched properties and projects, a red dot for new matches and the status. Enterprise brands get **My demands / Team demands** |
| **Leads** | Contact requests received and numbers viewed (Flow 11) |
| **Enquiries** | What the brand sent: Numbers you've viewed, Contacts requested (with Pending, Accepted, Rejected), Images requested, Projects enquired |

Drafts appear here as "Unfinished listings — pick up where you left off", with Resume and Discard.

- A deactivated account shows an amber banner. A self-deactivated brand sees a reactivate option. A brand deactivated by Keydemand sees "Your account has been deactivated by Keydemand".

---

###### Flow 13 — Manage a demand (open, edit, deactivate, reactivate, delete)

- **Actor:** The poster, or any user of an enterprise brand.
- **Prerequisites:** The demand exists.
1. Open the demand from the dashboard. The owner bar offers **Edit**, **Deactivate** (or **Activate**), **Delete**, **Download as PDF** and **Copy link**. Enterprise brands also see **Ask my RM**.
2. **Edit:** the same form opens with stored values. After the first enquiry arrives, **four fields lock**: asset class, transaction type, city and location. Everything else stays editable. Locked fields rejected on save are reported by name.
3. **Deactivate:** a confirmation pop-up. The demand leaves matching. Open requests on it close. Its high-value lead, if any, is withdrawn. A receipt appears.
4. **Activate:** "Demand activated". A demand still waiting for approval cannot be switched on: "This demand is waiting for Keydemand approval and cannot be switched on yet."
5. **Delete:** a confirmation pop-up. "Demand deleted". Open requests close. The free slot is **not** given back.
6. **Fulfilled:** the system supports marking a demand fulfilled, which closes requests and withdraws the lead. The web app does not show a Fulfilled button on the demand page.

**Rules**

- Demands do not expire under the current matching rules.
- An unauthorised person who opens an edit link is sent back to the demand page.
- A Keydemand member can edit only on accounts whose team they are on. Other edits happen in the Control Panel.

---

###### Flow 14 — Demand audience ("Who can see this")

- A Brand's demand is visible to **agents and the Keydemand team**. The Brand has no control.
- An agent cannot reveal or enquire on a brand demand unless agents are in its audience.
- A demand routed as high-value (Flow 15) drops agents until Keydemand releases it.
- A release adds agents back only if the poster's stored choice included them. If not, the release is refused: "Agents not chosen".
- Agents who see a brand's demand through matching see it as a **verified requirement**. They never browse the brand's demand list.

---

###### Flow 15 — High-value and Keydemand-managed routing

- **Actor:** The system; then the Keydemand team.
- **Prerequisites:** A live brand demand.
1. After posting, the system checks the demand against the **High Value Lead rules**: the city must be one of eight major cities (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi), the asset class and transaction type must match a rule, and the demand size must reach the rule's minimum.
2. If it qualifies, the demand is **hidden from agents** and a **High Value Lead** is opened and assigned to Keydemand members. They are told "A demand in [city] now qualifies as high-value and has been assigned to you."
3. **What the brand sees:** nothing special. The demand looks normal in its own dashboard. Nobody tells the brand the word "high-value".
4. Keydemand contacts the brand directly.
5. If the demand is edited or the rules change, the lead is re-checked. A demand that stops qualifying is released and its lead is **Withdrawn**.
6. Ending the demand (delete, deactivate, fulfil) withdraws the lead in every state.

**Rules**

- Demands posted by agents are exempt.
- Managed Space demands are handled differently and are not part of this check.
- When Keydemand later releases the lead, only subscribed agents with a matching live property are told.

---

###### Flow 16 — How matching and the % Match score work

- **Actor:** The system.
- **Prerequisites:** A live, approved demand.

**What the brand sees:** Matched properties and projects appear on the demand card, in the dashboard, and in the 6 pm summary, each with a percentage.

**Step 1 — hidden or shown:** A listing is hidden if it is not live, the asset class does not go with the demand (Retail and F&B go together), the transaction differs, the city differs, it is more than 3 km from every requested location, the area is below 75% or above 125% of the request, or (Retail and F&B) the ceiling is more than 1 ft lower than asked.

**Step 2 — the percentage:** Each asset class has its own weights. A requirement the demand did not ask for counts in full. A requirement the demand asked for that the property leaves blank earns nothing.

| Row | Retail weight | F&B weight |
| :---- | :---: | :---: |
| Location | 20 | 18.75 |
| Area | 20 | 18.75 |
| Ceiling height | 20 | 18.75 |
| Floor | 20 | 18.75 |
| Fit-outs | 5 | 5 |
| Possession | 5 | 5 |
| Frontage | 5 | 5 |
| Store type | 5 | 0 |
| Cooking type | — | 5 |
| Non-veg | — | 5 |

**Step 3:** Matches below **50%** are left out of lists, counts and the digest. Results are sorted best first. Ties go to the nearer listing, then the most recently updated.

**Not scored:** price (even if the demand has a budget), washroom, parking, mezzanine, OC, lease terms, building age.

**Other rules**

- Projects are matched on class, transaction, city, unit size range (10% below the smallest to 20% above the largest) and the 3 km rule.
- The brand's own listings may match (not applicable to brands, who post no properties).
- A new match is highlighted until the brand opens it.

---

###### Flow 17 — Projects and "Show Interest"

- **Actor:** A brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in to submit interest in one tap.
1. Open a project from Explore (Projects), a rail, or a demand's relevant projects.
2. Press **Show Interest**. The profile details are sent automatically. A pop-up says "Thank you for showing interest." The button then reads as already sent.
3. A signed-out visitor sees a short enquiry form instead.
4. The interest goes to the project's Keydemand Relationship Manager. The developer's contact is not revealed.
5. **Dashboard → Enquiries → Projects enquired** lists every project the brand reached out to.
6. A project can also be downloaded as a PDF when signed in. Signed out: "Sign in to download this project as a PDF".

---

###### Flow 18 — Saved (favourites)

1. Tap the heart on a property or project card. Signed out, the visitor is asked to sign in first and the save then completes.
2. **Saved** has two tabs for a Brand: Properties and Projects. The Demands tab does not appear.
3. Each tab shows the count and the same cards as search.

---

###### Flow 19 — Notifications centre and preferences

- **Actor:** A brand user.
1. The bell shows an unread count. **Notifications** has **All** and **Unread** tabs and **Mark all read**.
2. Each row has a call-to-action button that opens the related page.
3. **Profile → Notifications** has switches for **Email**, **WhatsApp** and (mobile app only) **Push**.
4. Email shows only when the account has an email address.
5. **Enterprise brands:** Email and WhatsApp are off and locked, with the line "Off for enterprise accounts — your Keydemand team contacts you directly". Only in-app and push continue.
6. Only promotional messages can be switched off. Messages about requests, relevance and leads are always sent.
7. The 6 pm India-time summary is one roll-up of new matches and other digest items. It is skipped when there is nothing to report.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Push blocked on the phone | "Blocked on this device — enable Notifications for Keydemand in your device settings" |
| Push turn-off | "Push notifications turned off on this device" |
| WhatsApp switch fails | "Could not update WhatsApp preference" |

---

###### Flow 20 — View and edit the profile

- **Actor:** A brand user.
1. **Profile** shows Personal Details (name, mobile, official email, designation) and Business Details (company name, experience), plus Preferences (asset class and city).
2. **Edit Profile** allows: name, email, photo, designation, cities, brand description, company name, experience, and notification choices.
3. The **mobile number cannot be changed**. The asset class is locked to the brand's own.
4. Email is required and must be valid. Errors: "Email is required for this account" and "Email is not a valid address".
5. Saving asks "Save these changes?". Cancelling with edits asks "Discard your changes?".
6. A **Verified** badge shows beside the name. Enterprise brands also show an **Enterprise** badge.

---

###### Flow 21 — Deactivate and reactivate the account

- **Actor:** An individual brand user.
- **Prerequisites:** Individual account.
1. **Profile → More → Deactivate account**. A pop-up asks "Deactivate account?".
2. On confirm: the user's listings are hidden, their demands are taken down, and they stop showing as active.
3. On the next sign-in a pop-up offers **Reactivate account** or **Not now**. A **Reactivate account** button also sits on the Profile page.
4. Reactivating restores only what this deactivation hid. Demands a Keydemand member or the system hid separately stay hidden.
5. Deactivated by Keydemand: the user cannot reactivate. The message says "Your account was deactivated by Keydemand. Please contact support."

**Enterprise accounts:** The server refuses: "Enterprise and Keydemand-team accounts are managed by the Keydemand team — please contact your relationship manager." The Profile page can still show the button to an enterprise brand (see Section 7).

---

###### Flow 22 — Request account deletion

- **Actor:** An individual brand user.
1. **Profile → More → Delete Account**. A pop-up shows Full Name, Phone and Email read-only, an optional **Reason for leaving** list, and a tick to confirm.
2. Submit. The account is **queued for review**, not wiped on the spot. The words on screen say "request" for that reason.
3. The Delete Account page explains what is **Removed**, what is **Taken offline** and what is **Retained where required**.
4. The user can withdraw the request: "Cancel your deletion request?" then "Deletion request withdrawn".
5. Keydemand processes it from the Control Panel's Account Deletions list.

**Edge cases:** Enterprise accounts are refused. A second request while one is pending returns the first request's date. A request already processed cannot be withdrawn: "Your deletion request has already been processed."

---

###### Flow 23 — Help, Relationship Manager and assistance

- **Actor:** An enterprise brand user, or any brand.
1. **Help for everyone:** the Contact page lists the support email and phone, and the FAQs page answers common questions (hidden in the iPhone app).
2. **Relationship Manager card (enterprise):** name, designation, a **Call** button (phone number) and an **Email** button. Reach it from the profile menu entry **Relationship Manager**.
3. If no manager is assigned yet: "Your relationship manager will be assigned shortly", with the support email.
4. **Ask my RM** (enterprise brands, on a demand or on the card): choose **Edit, Deactivate, Delete, Activate or Other**. A note is optional, but **required for Other**: "Tell your RM what you need help with."
5. Sent: "Request sent — your Relationship Manager has been notified."
6. A second request for the same action on the same demand: "You already asked your RM about this — it is still open."
7. **Individual brands:** "Relationship Manager help is available to enterprise brands. Contact Keydemand to upgrade."

**System side-effects**

- The account's Keydemand team and the assigned manager are alerted. The manager gets in-app, email and WhatsApp.
- If no manager is assigned, an email goes to the operations inbox.
- Keydemand resolves the request in the Control Panel and the brand is told.

---

###### Flow 24 — Sign out

1. Use **Logout** from the profile menu.
2. The session ends on the device. Saved city and draft choices stay on the device.

Notes:

- Self-initiated actions (posting, editing, deleting) are receipts and do not count towards the daily cap. The cap is effectively unlimited today.
- Brands do not get "Your number was viewed" for their own demands, because they approve each request instead.
- Enterprise users never get WhatsApp or email.

##### 5. Limits and Rules

| Rule | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Free demands (individual) | 3 per brand, lifetime |
| Free contact reveals (individual) | 5 per user, lifetime |
| Enterprise | Unlimited demands and reveals |
| One-time code | 6 digits |
| Enquiry and contact-request expiry | 72 hours |
| Hidden-photo request expiry | 72 hours |
| Fields locked after first enquiry response | Asset class, transaction type, city, location |
| Demand expiry | None under current rules |
| Match minimum | 50% |
| Match distance | 3 km from a requested location |
| Match area window | 75% to 125% of the request |
| Other nearby localities | Up to 3 |
| Digest time | 6 pm India time |
| High-value cities | Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi |
| Demand audience | Agents and Keydemand (fixed) |
| Brand explore scope | Retail, F&B, Office |
| Brand post scope | Own asset class only |
| Email for sign-up | Required, format and mail-server checked |
| Account deactivate or delete | Individual only |

### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Older sheet says the number is sent over WhatsApp and not shown; the app shows it in a pop-up with Copy and Call buttons (verified in code, differs from older sheet).
- Older sheet gives suppliers 4 working days; requests expire after 72 hours.
- Older sheet says enterprise teammates cannot edit each other's demands; since 2026-10-03 every user of an enterprise brand manages every demand.
- Older sheet says enterprise can deactivate; the server refuses, and the Profile page may still show the button to enterprise brands because the screen cannot tell the brand kind.
- The role picker card says "Post 1 demand" but the real free limit is three.

## Office-Tenant-Journey.md  [AUTHORITATIVE]
**Source:** Markdown file · ID `1pW1t16J88AlsucY7Sj7SI9TdJTXqQIp5` · owner arvind.m@futuristglobal.com · modified 2026-11-04 · 41,929 bytes · persona: Office Tenant · read coverage: 100% (copied below byte for byte from the build copy `~/Documents/Keydemand_docs/office-tenant-journey/Office-Tenant-Journey.md`, which has the same byte size as the Drive file; only the heading levels are nested) · published with screenshots as "Office Journey with Screenshots.pdf" (PDF `1su_p-SBfUsHpVwhfMTrLQC1HY4K2uCid`) · this is the app-checked revision of "Office Tenant - Individual and Enterprise Complete Journey-Product Documentation.md" (`1vC7onuRyZW0mEgewGvG-r20yzPrfzydY`, pradeepa.pv@futuristglobal.com, modified 2026-11-01, 42,338 bytes); differences from that earlier text: compared word for word on 2026-11-06 with the build folder's copy of that earlier text (`source.md`): 3 `&nbsp;` markers removed; cross-reference number "7" changed to "6" in 5 places; cross-reference number "11" changed to "27"; nothing else differs.

### Content
#### Persona 04 — Office Tenant, Individual and Enterprise

---

##### 1. Persona Snapshot

###### Who they are

An **Office Tenant** is a company looking to lease or buy office space. The same role also covers a tenant who is open to **managed (co-working) space**. Tenants post requirements ("demands") and browse supply. They never post properties.

|  | Individual Tenant | Enterprise Tenant |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **How they join** | Self-serve: phone number, one-time code, one short form | Set up offline by the Keydemand team, usually for large or repeat requirements |
| **Who logs in** | One person | Several people from the same company, each with their own number |
| **Demands** | 1 free, for life | Unlimited |
| **Contact reveals** | 5 free, for life | Unlimited |
| **Who handles the demands** | The tenant and the agent market | The Keydemand team. Demands are Keydemand-managed |
| **Relationship Manager** | None | A dedicated Keydemand manager, shown on the profile |
| **WhatsApp and email** | On (can be switched off) | Always off. In-app and push only |
| **Deactivate or delete own account** | Yes | Can. But must contact the Relationship Manager |

###### Goals

- State an office requirement once and see matching buildings.
- Reach landlords and brokers fast.
- For big requirements, hand the search to Keydemand.

###### What an Office Tenant can and cannot do

| Can | Cannot |
| :---- | :---- |
| Post an Office demand | Post properties |
| Post a Managed Space demand (unless switched off at sign-up) | Browse other people's demands (Keydemand staff only) |
| Explore Office **and** Managed Space properties and projects | Buy an agent subscription |
| Reveal supplier phone numbers (5 free) | Open the Leads page (staff only) |
| Request hidden photos | Choose who can see the demand (fixed: agents and Keydemand) |
| Show interest in projects | Approve or decline contact requests (numbers reveal at once) |
| Tick "Also interested in Managed Space" |  |

###### Limits and paywalls at a glance

| Limit | Individual | Enterprise |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Demands | 1 per person, for life. The first is posted at sign-up | Unlimited |
| Contact reveals | 5 per person, for life | Unlimited |
| What happens at the limit | A full-screen prompt to explore Enterprise Solution | Not applicable |

###### Asset-class scope

| Action | Scope |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Post a demand** | Office and Managed Space. Office only if the tenant unticks "Also interested in Managed Space" at sign-up, or Keydemand switches it off |
| **Explore properties and projects** | Office and Managed Space |
| **Cannot see** | Retail and F&B |

The one free demand is shared. A tenant who posts an Office demand has no free demand left for Managed Space.

---

##### 2. Screen and Navigation Map

###### Where the menu items appear

| Surface | Items shown to an Office Tenant |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Desktop top bar** | Explore Properties, Post Demand, Enterprise Solution |
| **Desktop profile menu** | Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager (enterprise only), Saved, Notifications |
| **Phone drawer** | Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager (enterprise only), Saved, Notifications, Explore Properties, Post Demand, Enterprise Solution |
| **Phone bottom bar** | Home, Explore, Dashboard, Menu |
| **Menu tab (mobile app)** | Explore properties, Projects, Saved, Post Demand, Dashboard, Profile, Relationship Manager, Notifications, Enterprise Solution, About Us, Our Clients, Investors, Contact Us, FAQs, Privacy, Terms, Cookie Policy |

**Never shown:** Post Property, Explore Demands, Subscription, Leads, Agent Subscription, List Project (guests only).

###### Screens

| Screen | Purpose | Gate |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Home | City feed: featured projects, new properties, exclusive projects, developer projects | Public |
| Search / Explore | Properties and projects with filters | Public (photos hidden when signed out) |
| Property and project detail | Full listing, contact reveal, hidden-photo request, Show Interest, PDF, save | Public (limited) |
| Post Demand | The shared requirement form | Signed in. Blocked by the limit prompt when the free demand is used |
| Demand detail | Own demand, matches, edit, deactivate, delete, PDF, share | Owner (or company team for enterprise) |
| Dashboard | Overview, Demands, Leads, Enquiries | Signed in |
| Saved | Saved properties and projects | Signed in |
| Notifications | Notification centre | Signed in |
| Profile and Edit Profile | Details, notification switches, deactivate, delete | Signed in |
| Enterprise Solution | Enquiry form | Public. **Hidden inside the iPhone app** |
| Delete Account | Deletion request form | Signed in |

###### Mobile versus desktop

- The profile is a page on desktop and a drawer entry on phones.
- The iPhone app hides all sales prompts. A limit prompt shows the limit only, with a Close button.
- Push notifications exist only in the mobile apps.

---

##### 3. End-to-End Flows

###### Flow 1 — Sign up as an Office Tenant

- **Actor:** A new tenant representative.
- **Prerequisites:** An Indian mobile number that can receive SMS. Nobody has registered with it before.

**Steps**

1. Open **Sign in** ("Welcome aboard"). Enter the 10-digit number. Tick the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy box. Press **Continue**.
2. Errors: "Enter your mobile number." / "Enter a valid 10-digit number." / "Please accept the Terms of Use & Privacy Policy to continue."
3. The system finds no account. **Choose your role** shows four cards. Pick **Office / Managed Space Tenant**.
4. A second screen, **What best describes you?**, offers **Office Tenant** ("Looking to lease/buy office or retail space for my business") and **Managed Space Tenant** ("Looking for co-working or managed workspace seats"). Pick **Office Tenant**.
5. A six-digit code is sent by SMS. Enter it. It submits on the sixth digit.
6. The **Post your requirement** form opens: "Tell us about the office space you need".
7. Fill the starred fields, tick consent and submit. A pop-up lists any missing field.
8. The location is checked against the chosen city before anything is created. If wrong: "Check the location" — "[Place] is in [City], outside [Selected city]. Pick a location inside [Selected city]."
9. The account and the first demand are created together. The **You're in!** screen says "Your requirement has been posted. Our team will match you with verified office spaces." The button reads **See matches for your requirement**.

**Registration form fields (Office Tenant)**

| Field | Required | Notes |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |
| Your Name | Yes |  |
| Company Name | Yes | Shown as the tenant's company |
| Official Email ID | Yes | Format, disposable domain and mail-server checks |
| City | Yes |  |
| Location / Area | Yes | Picked from map search. Must sit inside the city |
| Transaction Type | Yes | Lease or Buy |
| Carpet Area (sq. ft.) | Yes | One number |
| Possession Needed | Yes | Immediate, Within 3, 6 or 9 months, After 9 months |
| Also interested in Managed Space Offices | No | Ticked by default |
| Terms consent | Yes |  |

**System side-effects**

- The account is created as an **individual** Office Tenant with the company name stored.
- The tick for managed space is saved on the account. If it stays ticked, the tenant may post Managed Space demands later. If it is unticked, the tenant posts Office only.
- If ticked, a **Managed Office interest** lead is created for Keydemand, noting the tenant, city and demand reference. It appears in the Control Panel Enquiries list.
- The first demand goes to **agents and the Keydemand team** and uses up the **one free demand**.
- A **Welcome** message goes out (in-app, WhatsApp, email). WhatsApp and all notification types start on. Per the new notifications sheet (Section 4), Welcome goes by WhatsApp and toast only ("Welcome to Keydemand. Your account is active."), with a Complete profile CTA (Section 6, item 21).
- A tenant who stops after the code gets a **Profile incomplete** WhatsApp reminder 24 hours later. Per the new sheet this is called Onboarding incomplete and also shows the toast "Complete your profile for better recommendations." with a Complete profile CTA (Section 6, item 22).

**Edge cases**

| Situation | What the user sees |
| :---- | :---- |
| Wrong code | "That OTP is incorrect. Check the code and try again." |
| Old code | "Your code expired. Tap Resend for a new one." |
| Too many wrong codes | "Too many attempts. Request a new code." |
| Code requested too soon | "Please wait N seconds before requesting another OTP." The button counts down |
| Many requests | "Too many OTP requests. Try again in N seconds." |
| Registration session expired | "Your registration session has expired. Start again." |
| Number already registered | "An account with this mobile number already exists. Sign in instead." |
| Account created but demand failed | A yellow note: "Your account is ready, but your requirement was not saved. Post it again to start getting matches." Button: **Post your requirement** |
| Enterprise tenant tries to self-register | Not allowed. Use Enterprise Solution |

---

###### Flow 2 — Sign in (returning tenant)

- **Actor:** An existing tenant user.
- **Prerequisites:** An active account.

1. Enter the number and accept the consent tick. Continue.
2. Enter the six-digit code.
3. The user lands on the page they came from, or on Home.
4. Sessions refresh quietly. After a long idle period: "Your session has expired. Please sign in again."

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| User deactivated the account | A pop-up offers **Reactivate account** or **Not now** |
| Keydemand deactivated the account | A pop-up asks the user to contact support |
| Account deleted | "This account has been removed. Contact support." |

---

###### Flow 3 — Post a demand (Office)

- **Actor:** An Office Tenant, or any user of an enterprise tenant company.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. The free demand is unused (individual), or the tenant is enterprise.

**Steps**

1. Open **Post Demand**. The system first checks the free allowance. If used, the limit prompt stands in front of the form (Flow 5).
2. The form has a progress meter. The **asset class** shows Office and, if allowed, Managed Space.
3. Fill **Primary Details**, **Additional Details**, **Amenities**, **Transaction** (lease) and **Documents**.
4. Optional: save a draft. Leaving with unsaved edits asks "Save your draft before you go?". A returning user sees "Draft restored" with **Discard draft** and **Dismiss**.
5. Press **Post Office Demand**. A pop-up lists any missing required fields.
6. A confirmation appears and the demand opens in the dashboard.

**Field groups for an Office demand**

| Group | Fields |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Primary Details** | Transaction type (Lease or Buy), City, Location, Other interested locations (up to 3, optional), Map link (optional), Carpet area, Possession needed, **Budget** (rent per sq. ft. per month for lease), OC required |
| **Additional Details** | Age of property (Less than 5 years, 5–10, 10–20, Above 20, Any), Additional demand details (optional note) |
| **Amenities** | Washroom required, Car parking required, Bike parking required, **Fitout status** (Furnished or Unfurnished), and the office amenity picker (for example AC, Lift, Power backup, CCTV, Reception, Pantry, Vastu compliance, Reserved parking) |
| **Transaction (lease only)** | Lease tenure (years), Lock-in period (years). "Lock-in cannot be more than the lease tenure of N years." |
| **Documents** | Required documents the tenant expects from suppliers: Floor Plan, Autocad, Fire NOC, Other Licenses |

**Rules**

- **Required:** Transaction type, City, Location (picked from the list), Carpet area, Possession needed.
- **Audience:** Fixed to **agents and the Keydemand team**. The tenant cannot change it.
- **Card picture:** A stock picture for Office. A "Posted by" name is not offered to tenants (see Section 7).
- **Managed Space demands** use a shorter form (Flow 4).

**System side-effects**

- The free slot is used (individual tenants).
- The demand is checked for **high-value routing** (Flow 12).
- A Requirement posted receipt appears in-app. Per the new sheet, the Notification centre row and the toast both read "Requirement [ID] for [Type] in [Locality], [City] is live."
- **Production:** the demand waits for Keydemand approval before it is live. Test environments approve automatically.
- Matching starts as soon as it is live (Flow 13).

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Tenant tries Retail or F&B | "Your account cannot post this type of demand." |
| Managed Space chosen after unticking the managed-space interest | The class is not offered |
| Draft exists | Offered back next visit |
| Errors | Each problem is shown beside its field, all at once |

---

###### Flow 4 — Post a Managed Space demand

- **Actor:** An Office Tenant who is open to managed space.
- **Prerequisites:** Same as Flow 3. Managed space is only offered if the tenant did not turn the interest off.

1. In **Post Demand**, choose **Managed Space** as the asset class.
2. The form shrinks to one section, **Primary Details**: Transaction type (fixed to Lease), City, Location, Other interested locations, **Number of seats**, **Possession needed**.
3. **Number of seats** must be a whole number of **20 or more**. Messages: "Number of Seats is required" and "Enter 20 or more seats". The hint reads "Minimum 20 seats".
4. Possession offers only **Immediate** and **Within 3 months**.
5. Submit with **Post Managed Space Demand**.

**System side-effects**

- A Managed Space demand is marked **Keydemand-managed**. Keydemand handles it.
- A tenant's free demand is shared, so this uses the same single slot as an Office demand.
- Buying is not possible: "managed-space supports lease only".

---

###### Flow 5 — Hit the free demand limit and the Enterprise pitch

- **Actor:** An individual tenant with the free demand used.
- **Prerequisites:** One demand already posted.

1. The tenant opens **Post Demand**. The page does not open. A prompt stands in front.
2. The prompt says the account includes one free demand and pitches unlimited postings, priority matching with landlords and a dedicated Relationship Manager.
3. Buttons: **Explore Enterprise Solution** and **Back to Dashboard**.
4. If the tenant tries another route, the server refuses: "Free limit (1 demand) reached. Contact Keydemand for the enterprise package."
5. An in-app message also appears: "You have used your 1 requirement on this plan. Enroll for Enterprise Solution to post more." with Enroll. The new sheet changes the Notification centre copy to "You have exhausted all your listings. Enroll for Enterprise Solution to post more." with no CTA and no toast (Section 6, item 26).

**Rules**

- The count belongs to the **person**. It never goes back down: deleting the demand does not return the slot.
- Enterprise tenants skip the check.
- In the iPhone app the prompt shows the limit only.

---

###### Flow 6 — Enquire for Enterprise Solution

- **Actor:** Any visitor or tenant.
- **Prerequisites:** None. Not available in the iPhone app.

1. Open **Enterprise Solution** from the menu or from the limit prompt.
2. Fill: Full Name (required), Company (required), Work Email (optional), WhatsApp Number (required, +91), Primary City Focus, Brand Type (the form uses Retail, F&B, Office, Managed Space; a tenant's own type is pre-selected when signed in).
3. Press **Submit Enquiry**. "Thank you for your enquiry" appears with **Submit another enquiry**.
4. Failure: "Couldn't submit your enquiry — please try again."

**System side-effects**

- A sales lead is recorded as New and linked to the user if signed in.
- It appears in the Control Panel Enquiries list. A Keydemand member follows up offline.
- No account change happens automatically.

---

###### Flow 7 — Becoming an Enterprise Tenant (offline)

- **Actor:** The Keydemand team, then the tenant.
- **Prerequisites:** An enquiry, a direct request or sales outreach.

1. Keydemand and the company agree terms offline.
2. A Keydemand admin upgrades the tenant, adds colleagues' numbers under the same company, and assigns a Relationship Manager. Details: Control Panel guide.
3. Each colleague signs in with their own number.

**What changes**

| Area | Before | After |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Demands | 1 free | Unlimited |
| Contact reveals | 5 free | Unlimited |
| Demand handling | Open to matching as normal | **Keydemand-managed**: handled by Keydemand and shown to Keydemand only |
| Who manages demands | The poster | **Every user of the company** can read, edit, deactivate and delete all company demands |
| Help | Contact page | Relationship Manager card |
| WhatsApp and email | Optional | Off and locked |
| Deactivate or delete | Self-service | Only through Keydemand |

###### Flow 8 — Explore properties and projects

- **Actor:** An Office Tenant or a visitor.
- **Prerequisites:** None. Signed-in users see photos.

1. Open **Explore Properties**. The page opens on the saved city, in Office and Managed Space.
2. Switch between **Property** and **Projects**. A Demands option does not appear.
3. Use filters. Sort by Most Recent, Price: Low to High, Price: High to Low, or Area: Largest First.
4. Open a card for the full detail page.

| Filter group | Options |
| :---- | :---- |
| Listing type | Property, Projects |
| Transaction | Lease, Sale (Managed Space is lease only: the Sale option is disabled with that note) |
| Asset class | Office, Managed Space |
| Availability | Immediate, within 3, 6, 9 months |
| Fit-out | Furnished, unfurnished and similar |
| Amenities | Office amenity list |
| Facilities | Washroom, parking |
| Legal | OC status |
| Ranges | Area and price |
| Projects only | Project status, type, Mixed Use, number of seats, total project size |

**Edge cases**

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Tenant asks for Retail or F&B | Narrowed silently to Office and Managed Space |
| Signed out | Photos hidden. Contact reveal asks the visitor to sign in first |
| Listing limited to certain audiences | The tenant sees it only if a ticked group describes them (for example Office tenant or Enterprise tenant) |

###### Flow 9 — View a supplier's phone number

- **Actor:** An Office Tenant.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. The listing is live and visible to the tenant.

1. On a property, project or card, tap **View number**.
2. If signed out, the user signs in first, then the reveal continues.
3. The system checks: already revealed (free), own listing, listing live, audience allows the tenant, then the allowance.
4. The number reveals **at once** in a **Contact Unlocked** pop-up: the contact's name, the number, a **Copy** button and a **Call [first name]** button.
5. A free reveal is counted.
6. After five free reveals: the account includes 5 free contact views, and the prompt pitches Enterprise for unlimited reveals.

**System side-effects**

- A reveal record is saved.
- The owner is told, as an in-app "Someone viewed your contact" row and a line in the 6 pm summary.
- Enterprise tenants are never counted.

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Listing deactivated, deleted or not approved | "This listing is no longer available." |
| Own listing | "This is your own listing." |
| Hidden from the tenant's group | "Property not found" |
| Request closed because the listing ended | The free reveal is **given back** |

###### Flow 10 — Request hidden photos

- **Actor:** An Office Tenant.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. The owner marked some photos hidden.

1. Hidden photos show **Request images**.
2. A pop-up says **Image Request Sent** — "Awaiting owner approval". Button: **Got it**.
3. The owner is alerted with **Share images**.
4. **Approved:** "Images are now available for [ID]". The tenant sees every photo from then on.
5. **Declined:** "Your image request for [ID] was not approved." The request is closed. Per the new sheet, both outcomes also go by WhatsApp and to the Notification centre, with a View Property CTA (copy in Section 4).
6. No answer in 72 hours: the request expires.

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| A second request for the same listing | "You have already sent a request for this listing." |
| Own listing | "You cannot send a request on your own listing." |
| Listing ended first | "Your request was closed because the property is no longer available." |

---

###### Flow 11 — Leads, dashboard and enquiries

- **Actor:** An Office Tenant.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in. Tabs: **Overview, Demands, Leads, Enquiries**. No Properties tab.

| Tab | What it shows |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Overview** | Counts for Demands, Leads and Enquiries. Each opens its tab |
| **Demands** | The tenant's demand cards with matched properties and projects, a red dot for new matches, status. Enterprise tenants get **My demands / Team demands** |
| **Leads** | **Phone numbers viewed**: people who unlocked the tenant's number. Tapping a person shows their history. There is **no** contact-request inbox, because tenant numbers reveal at once |
| **Enquiries** | What the tenant sent: Numbers you've viewed, Contacts requested, Images requested, Projects enquired |

- Drafts appear as "Unfinished listings — pick up where you left off" with **Resume** and **Discard**.
- Demand responses and matches are viewed on the dashboard. There is no separate inbox.
- A deactivated account shows an amber banner with the right next step.

---

###### Flow 12 — High-value and Keydemand-managed routing

- **Actor:** The system, then the Keydemand team.
- **Prerequisites:** A live demand.

1. After posting, the system checks the demand against the **High Value Lead rules**: one of eight major cities (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi), a matching asset class and transaction type, and a demand size at or above the rule's minimum. Managed Space is excluded.
2. If it qualifies, the demand is **hidden from agents**, a **High Value Lead** is opened and assigned to Keydemand members, and they are alerted.
3. **What the tenant sees:** nothing special. The demand looks normal. Nobody says "high-value".
4. Keydemand contacts the tenant directly. When ready, Keydemand releases the lead. Agents are added back only if the tenant's stored choice included them.
5. If the demand is edited or the rules change, the lead is re-checked. A demand that stops qualifying is released and the lead is **Withdrawn**.
6. Ending the demand (delete, deactivate, fulfil) withdraws the lead.

**Other Keydemand-managed cases**

| Case | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Managed Space demand | Always Keydemand-managed |
| Enterprise tenant demand | Always Keydemand-managed |
| Office demand above a city's old size threshold | Treated as high-value when no rule matches |

Agent-posted demands are exempt from the high-value check.

---

###### Flow 13 — How matching and the % Match score work

- **Actor:** The system.
- **Prerequisites:** A live, approved demand.

**What the tenant sees:** Matched properties and projects appear on the demand card, the dashboard and the 6 pm summary, each with a percentage.

**Step 1 — hidden or shown.** A listing is hidden if it is not live; the asset class does not go with the demand (Office goes only with Office, Managed Space only with Managed Space); the transaction differs; the city differs; it is more than 3 km from every requested location; or the area is below 75% or above 125% of the request.

**Step 2 — the percentage.** Office weights are Location 40, Area 40, Fit-outs 15, Possession 5. Managed Space weights are Location, Possession and Seats, a third each. A requirement the demand did not ask for counts in full. A requirement it asked for that the supplier left blank earns nothing.

| Row | Full credit | Part credit |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Location | Same locality, or within 1 km | 0.8 for 1–2 km, 0.75 for 2–3 km |
| Area | Within 10% of the request | Half credit elsewhere in the 75–125% window |
| Fit-outs (office) | Furnished when furnished is asked | Half for landlord fit-out |
| Possession | Available in time | Half for one step late |
| Seats (managed) | Enough seats | Half for 75% or more of the seats |

**Step 3.** Matches below **50%** are left out. Results sort best first. Ties go to the nearer listing, then the most recently updated.

**Not scored:** price, washroom, parking, building age, floor band, cabins, meeting rooms, industries.

**Other rules**

- A managed centre project is relevant only to Managed Space demands. A mixed-use project is never relevant to them.
- Projects match on class, transaction, city, unit size range (10% below the smallest to 20% above the largest) and the 3 km rule.
- New matches are highlighted until opened.

###### Flow 14 — Manage a demand (open, edit, deactivate, reactivate, delete)

- **Actor:** The poster, or any user of an enterprise tenant company.

1. Open the demand from the dashboard. The owner bar offers **Edit**, **Deactivate** (or **Activate**), **Delete**, **Download as PDF** and **Copy link**.
2. **Edit:** the same form opens with stored values. After the first enquiry response, **four fields lock**: asset class, transaction type, city and location. Locked fields rejected on save are reported by name. Per the new sheet, a successful save shows the toast "Changes saved." and a Notification centre row: "Requirement [ID] for [Type] in [Locality], [City] has been edited successfully."
3. **Deactivate:** a confirmation pop-up. The demand leaves matching. Open requests close. Its high-value lead, if any, is withdrawn.
4. **Activate:** "Demand activated". A demand still waiting for approval cannot be switched on: "This demand is waiting for Keydemand approval and cannot be switched on yet."
5. **Delete:** confirm, then "Demand deleted". Open requests close. The free slot is **not** returned.
6. **Fulfilled:** the service supports it. The web demand page has no button for it.

**Rules**

- Demands do not expire under current matching rules.
- Someone who opens an edit link without permission is sent back to the demand page.

---

###### Flow 15 — Demand audience

- An Office Tenant's demand is visible to **agents and the Keydemand team**. The tenant has no control.
- An agent cannot reveal or enquire on a demand unless agents are in its audience.
- A high-value demand drops agents until Keydemand releases it. A release is refused ("Agents not chosen") if the stored choice excluded agents.
- Agents see matched demands only through their own listings, never as a browse list.

---

###### Flow 16 — Projects and "Show Interest"

1. Open a project from Explore (Projects), a rail or a demand's relevant projects.
2. Press **Show Interest**. The profile details go out automatically. A pop-up says "Thank you for showing interest." Per the new sheet, the tenant also gets the toast "Interest shown successfully." and a Notification centre row: "You have successfully shown interest in [project name]." The button then reads as already sent.
3. A signed-out visitor sees a short enquiry form instead.
4. The interest goes to the project's Keydemand Relationship Manager. The developer's contact is not revealed.
5. **Dashboard → Enquiries → Projects enquired** lists every project reached.
6. PDF download needs sign-in: "Sign in to download this project as a PDF".

---

###### Flow 17 — Saved

1. Tap the heart on a property or project. Signed out, the visitor signs in first and the save then completes.
2. **Saved** shows two tabs: Properties and Projects. The Demands tab does not appear.

---

###### Flow 18 — Notifications centre and preferences

1. The bell shows an unread count. **Notifications** has **All** and **Unread** tabs and **Mark all read**. Each row has a call-to-action.
2. **Profile → Notifications** has switches for **Email**, **WhatsApp** and (mobile app only) **Push**. Email shows only when an address is on file.
3. **Enterprise tenants:** Email and WhatsApp are off and locked: "Off for enterprise accounts — your Keydemand team contacts you directly". In-app and push continue.
4. Only promotional messages can be switched off. Messages about requests and leads are always sent.
5. A 6 pm India-time summary rolls up new matches. It is skipped when there is nothing to report.

| Situation | Result |
| :---- | :---- |
| Push blocked on the phone | "Blocked on this device — enable Notifications for Keydemand in your device settings" |
| Push turned off | "Push notifications turned off on this device" |
| WhatsApp switch fails | "Could not update WhatsApp preference" |

---

###### Flow 19 — View and edit the profile

1. **Profile** shows Personal Details (name, mobile, official email, designation or about), Business Details (company name) and Preferences (city).
2. **Edit Profile** allows: name, email, photo, "about yourself", cities, transaction types, company name and notification choices.
3. The **mobile number cannot be changed**.
4. Email is required and must be valid: "Email is required for this account" and "Email is not a valid address".
5. Saving asks "Save these changes?". Cancelling with edits asks "Discard your changes?".
6. A **Verified** badge shows beside the name. Enterprise tenants also show an **Enterprise** badge.

---

###### Flow 20 — Deactivate and reactivate the account

- **Actor:** An individual tenant.

1. **Profile → More → Deactivate account**, then confirm "Deactivate account?".
2. The tenant's listings are hidden, their demands are taken down, and they stop showing as active.
3. At the next sign-in a pop-up offers **Reactivate account** or **Not now**. A **Reactivate account** button also sits on the Profile page.
4. Reactivating restores only what this deactivation hid.
5. If Keydemand deactivated the account the tenant cannot reactivate: "Your account was deactivated by Keydemand. Please contact support."

**Enterprise tenants:** The profile hides the buttons. If forced, the server refuses: "Enterprise and Keydemand-team accounts are managed by the Keydemand team — please contact your relationship manager." A tenant in a company with more than one tenant counts as enterprise.

---

###### Flow 21 — Request account deletion

1. **Profile → More → Delete Account**. A pop-up shows Full Name, Phone and Email read-only, an optional **Reason for leaving**, and a tick to confirm.
2. Submit. The account is **queued for review**, not wiped immediately.
3. The Delete Account page explains what is **Removed**, **Taken offline** and **Retained where required**.
4. The tenant can withdraw it: "Cancel your deletion request?" then "Deletion request withdrawn".
5. Keydemand processes it from the Control Panel's Account Deletions list.

**Edge cases:** Enterprise tenants are refused. A request already processed cannot be withdrawn: "Your deletion request has already been processed."

---

###### Flow 22 — Help and Relationship Manager

1. **Everyone:** the Contact page lists support email and phone. FAQs answer common questions (hidden in the iPhone app).
2. **Enterprise tenants:** the **Relationship Manager** menu entry opens a card with the manager's name, designation, a **Call** button and an **Email** button.
3. If no manager is assigned yet: "Your relationship manager will be assigned shortly", with the support email.
4. The in-app **Ask my RM** button and its note box are available to enterprise **brands** only. Tenants contact the manager directly (see Section 7).

---

###### Flow 23 — Sign out

1. Use **Logout** from the profile menu.
2. The session ends on the device.

##### 5. Limits and Rules

| Rule | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Free demands (individual) | 1 per person, lifetime. Shared between Office and Managed Space |
| Free contact reveals (individual) | 5 per person, lifetime |
| Enterprise | Unlimited demands and reveals |
| One-time code | 6 digits |
| Enquiry and image-request expiry | 72 hours |
| Fields locked after first response | Asset class, transaction type, city, location |
| Managed Space seats | Whole number, 20 or more |
| Managed Space transaction | Lease only |
| Managed Space possession | Immediate or within 3 months |
| Demand expiry | None under current rules |
| Match minimum | 50% |
| Match distance | 3 km |
| Match area window | 75% to 125% |
| Other nearby localities | Up to 3 |
| Digest time | 6 pm India time |
| Demand audience | Agents and Keydemand (fixed) |
| Post scope | Office, Managed Space (Office only if managed-space interest is off) |
| Explore scope | Office, Managed Space |
| Account deactivate or delete | Individual only |

### Business rules extracted
- **BR-PD-0832** — An Office Tenant is a company looking to lease or buy office space; the same role also covers a tenant open to managed (co-working) space. Tenants post demands and browse supply but never post properties. _(§ 1. Persona Snapshot › Who they are)_
- **BR-PD-0833** — An Individual Tenant joins self-serve with phone number, one-time code and one short form; an Enterprise Tenant is set up offline by the Keydemand team. _(§ 1 › Who they are table)_
- **BR-PD-0834** — Individual Tenant: one person logs in; Enterprise Tenant: several people from the same company log in, each with their own number. _(§ 1 › Who they are table)_
- **BR-PD-0835** — Individual Tenant gets 1 free demand for life; Enterprise gets unlimited demands. _(§ 1 › Who they are table)_
- **BR-PD-0836** — Individual Tenant gets 5 free contact reveals for life; Enterprise gets unlimited contact reveals. _(§ 1 › Who they are table)_
- **BR-PD-0837** — Individual tenant demands are handled by the tenant and the agent market; Enterprise demands are Keydemand-managed. _(§ 1 › Who they are table)_
- **BR-PD-0838** — Individual tenants have no Relationship Manager; Enterprise tenants have a dedicated Keydemand manager shown on the profile. _(§ 1 › Who they are table)_
- **BR-PD-0839** — For individual tenants WhatsApp and email notifications are on by default and can be switched off; for enterprise they are always off (in-app and push only). _(§ 1 › Who they are table)_
- **BR-PD-0840** — Individual tenants can deactivate or delete their own account; enterprise tenants must contact the Relationship Manager. _(§ 1 › Who they are table)_
- **BR-PD-0841** — An Office Tenant can post an Office demand and a Managed Space demand (unless managed space was switched off at sign-up). _(§ 1 › Can / Cannot)_

### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Notifications missing from the new sheet (Requirement deactivated/deleted, Request closed, 6 pm daily summary, 90-day "Confirm or update"): confirm whether they stay or are retired (item 24).

- Onboarding incomplete: sheet adds a toast; build sends WhatsApp only (item 22).
- Instant match alerts (WhatsApp, centre row, toast, View Relevancy) in the sheet are not built; build only rolls matches into the 6 pm summary (item 23).
- "Free listing available" row uses "listing" and "Upload listing" CTA; Post demand probably meant; reminder while free demand unused is not built (item 25).
- Free plan exhausted copy differs between sheet and build (item 26).
- My phone number viewed: sheet describes an approve-to-share contact request, which contradicts the built instant reveal ("no contact-request inbox", "numbers reveal at once"); [buyer / tenant / agent] placeholder needs a rule; "See who" CTA points to a Keydemand-only route (item 27).
- Image request declined copy differs by channel ("is rejected" vs "was not approved") (item 28).
- Project interest receipt (centre row and toast) in sheet is not built; build shows only the pop-up (item 29).
- Push channel: sheet has no push column; build sends push for image request answered, request closed and daily summary (item 30).

- Flow 1 step 4 describes Office Tenant as "lease/buy office or retail space", while Retail/F&B demands are refused for this persona.
- Section 7 is referenced ("Posted by", Ask my RM) but does not exist in this doc.
