### Content
#### Persona 06 — Developer

---

##### 1. Persona Snapshot

###### Who they are

A **Developer** is a real-estate company that builds commercial projects and wants them promoted on Keydemand. A developer is a **Keydemand-managed** persona. The developer does not run a self-service account. Keydemand staff create the developer's projects for them and handle every enquiry through a **Relationship Manager (RM)**.

|  | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **How they join** | They fill a short **List your project** form. This files a **lead**. No account is created. A Keydemand member calls them, then creates and approves the account in the Control Panel |
| **How they sign in** | Mobile number and a six-digit code, **only after** Keydemand has approved the account |
| **What they see after sign-in** | One screen only: **My Account** |
| **Projects** | Created and edited by Keydemand staff on the developer's behalf |
| **Demands, properties, enquiries, contact reveals** | None. The developer has no free allowances to count |
| **Notifications in the app** | None reachable. Email is the channel that lands |

###### Goals

- Get the company's projects in front of agents, brands and tenants.
- Receive interested buyers and tenants through Keydemand.
- Keep one named contact at Keydemand.

###### What a Developer can and cannot do

| Can | Cannot |
| :---- | :---- |
| Submit a **List your project** request (as a guest) | Post properties or demands |
| Sign in once approved | Explore, search or open any listing |
| See and edit their own name, email and designation | Open the dashboard, saved items, notifications or leads |
| Upload a profile photo | Reveal phone numbers or send enquiries |
| See their Relationship Manager's name, phone and email | Create or edit their own projects |
| Sign out | Deactivate or delete their own account |
|  | Change their mobile number |

###### Limits and paywalls at a glance

There are no free limits to hit. Every feature that has a limit is blocked outright for this persona.

###### Asset-class scope

None for posting or exploring. Projects created for a developer can serve **Retail and F&B**, **Office**, or both, and can be **Mixed Use**. See Flow 7.

---

##### 2. Screen and Navigation Map

###### Menu

A signed-in developer sees one destination.

| Surface | Items shown |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Desktop profile menu** | Account, Relationship Manager |
| **Phone drawer** | Account, Relationship Manager |
| **Phone bottom bar** | Home and Menu only (Explore and Dashboard are hidden) |
| **Menu tab (mobile app)** | Account, Relationship Manager, plus the public information links (About Us, Our Clients, Investors, Contact Us, FAQs, Privacy, Terms, Cookie Policy). Opening an information page sends the developer back to Account |

**Hidden for developers:** Dashboard, Profile, Saved, Notifications, Explore Properties, Projects, Post Property, Post Demand, Subscription, Leads, Enterprise Solution.

**For guests** (before approval) the top bar and drawer show **List Project**.

###### Screens

| Screen | Purpose | Gate |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| List your project | The lead form | Public (guests only in the menu) |
| Sign in and code screens | Sign in | Public |
| **My Account** | Name, phone, email, designation, company, city, photo, Relationship Manager card | Signed-in developer |
| Information pages (Contact, About, FAQs and so on) | Public content | Public. A signed-in developer who opens them is sent back to My Account |

###### How the lockdown works

- Right after sign-in, the app sends the developer to **My Account**.
- Any other page the developer opens redirects there. The sign-in pages are the only exception.
- The server enforces the same rule. Any request other than the allowed ones fails with "This account has no access to that feature."
- **Allowed requests:** read and edit own profile, read the Relationship Manager card, sign in, sign out, refresh the session, health checks, documentation, and error reports.

###### Mobile versus desktop

- On phones the **Relationship Manager** entry jumps to the card on My Account. On desktop the card sits under the header of the same page.
- The card offers a **Call** button that dials on phones.

---

##### 3. End-to-End Flows

###### Flow 1 — Submit "List your project" (guest)

- **Actor:** A developer representative, not yet a user.
- **Prerequisites:** A mobile number that can receive SMS. No account exists on it, or an approved developer account exists.

**How they get there:** **List Project** in the top bar or drawer (guests only), the page at the List your project address, or an old link that opens it as a pop-up. Developers and operators are **not** offered on the normal Choose-your-role screen.

**Steps**

1. **Step 1 — Role.** Choose **Developer** ("List your residential or commercial projects") or **Managed Space Operator**. The step bar shows Role, Verify, Details.
2. **Step 2 — Phone.** Enter the 10-digit mobile number. The system checks whether it is known. A new number locks the role and sends an SMS code. A known number gets a code without choosing a role.
3. **Step 3 — Code.** Enter the six-digit code. It submits on the sixth digit. A resend button counts down.
4. **Step 4 — Details.** Fill the form below.
5. Press submit. A **Request submitted** screen appears: "Thank you for sharing the information, our team will reach out to you shortly." with the line **A representative will call you** and a **Got it** button.

**Details form**

| Field | Required | Notes |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |
| Full Name | Yes | Up to 150 characters |
| Company Name | Yes | Up to 150 characters |
| Your Designation | Yes | For example "VP — Commercial Leasing" |
| Official Email ID | Yes | Format, disposable domain and mail-server checks. "Please enter a valid email address" |
| Phone Number | Pre-filled | The verified number |
| Select City | Yes |  |
| GST Number | No | A 15-character GSTIN or 21-character CIN. "GST / CIN is not valid - a 15-character GSTIN or a 21-character CIN" |

If a required field is empty, a pop-up lists exactly which ones.

**System side-effects**

- A **lead** is recorded with the source "developer onboarding" and status **New**. **No user account is created.**
- A repeat submission from the same number and role, while the lead is still New or Contacted, **updates that lead** and adds one to its submission count. It is not a duplicate.
- An email goes to Keydemand operations: "New Enquiry Alert — developer, [city]".
- The number is marked as a completed sign-up so no "profile incomplete" reminder is sent.
- The lead appears in the Control Panel Enquiries list.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | What the user sees |
| :---- | :---- |
| Wrong code | "That OTP is incorrect. Check the code and try again." |
| Old code | "Your code expired. Tap Resend for a new one." |
| Too many wrong codes | "Too many attempts. Request a new code." |
| Code requested too soon | "Please wait N seconds before requesting another OTP." The button counts down |
| Number could not be verified | "We could not verify this number. Please go back and re-send the code." |
| Someone who signed up under the old process and awaits review | "We already have your request — our team will contact you shortly." |
| Number previously not approved | "This number cannot list a project online. Please contact [support@keydemand.in](mailto:support@keydemand.in)." |
| Number belongs to an agent, brand or tenant | The form is refused: "This form is for developers and managed space operators" |
| Signed-in approved developer | The session proves the number. No code is needed. The role is taken from the account |
| Submit fails | A red message under the form with the server's reason |

---

###### Flow 2 — Wait for Keydemand and what the developer experiences

- **Actor:** The developer, waiting.
- **Prerequisites:** A lead exists (Flow 1).

1. The developer is **not signed in** and has no account yet.
2. A Keydemand member is assigned the lead and calls the developer. Lead statuses are **New, Contacted, Closed, Converted**.
3. If the developer tries to sign in before an account exists, the number is treated as new and the normal role picker appears. It does not offer the Developer card. A person who registered under the old process sees the approval message in Flow 4.
4. The developer receives no message from the app. Keydemand reaches out by phone or email.

---

###### Flow 3 — Keydemand creates the developer account (summary)

- **Actor:** A Keydemand admin.
- **Prerequisites:** A lead, and permission to add users. Full steps are in the Control Panel guide.

1. The admin opens **User Management → Developers** and adds the developer: name, phone, company name, designation, city, official email, and (optionally) GST or CIN.
2. A company record and the developer account are created together. The account is **pre-approved**, so the developer can sign in straight away.
3. If a legacy pending sign-up already exists for the same number and role, it is **approved and updated** instead of failing.
4. The admin marks the lead **Converted** and links the new account.
5. Keydemand assigns an **Account Handler** (the developer's Relationship Manager).

**Rules**

- Only Keydemand can approve or reject a pending developer: "Account is already approved; cannot change status" and "Account is already [status]" guard repeat changes.
- Rejecting leaves the developer unable to sign in.
- Email addresses are checked on every create and edit.

---

###### Flow 4 — Sign in as a developer

- **Actor:** An approved developer.
- **Prerequisites:** The account is approved and active.

1. Open **Sign in**. Enter the mobile number and accept the consent tick. Continue.
2. Enter the six-digit code.
3. The app lands on **My Account**.

**Edge cases**

| Situation | What the user sees |
| :---- | :---- |
| Waiting for approval | "Account pending Keydemand team review. Approved within 24 hours." (the app's wording library says "Your Keydemand team access is awaiting approval.") |
| Not approved | "Account registration was not approved. Contact support." (the library says "Your Keydemand team access was not approved.") |
| Deactivated by the developer | The system does not let a developer deactivate their own account |
| Deactivated by Keydemand | A pop-up asks the developer to contact support |
| Deleted | "This account has been removed. Contact support." |
| Wrong, old or repeated codes | Same messages as Flow 1 |

---

###### Flow 5 — Use My Account

- **Actor:** A signed-in developer.
- **Prerequisites:** Signed in.

1. **My Account** shows the developer's name, company and photo, then the **Relationship Manager** card, then **Account details**.
2. Press **Edit** to change **Name**, **Email** and **Designation**. Press **Save changes** or **Cancel**.
3. Messages: "Profile updated", "Name cannot be empty", "Could not update profile".
4. The photo can be changed with the avatar uploader.
5. Read-only rows: Name, Phone, Email, Designation, Company, City.
6. **The mobile number cannot be changed.**

**Rules**

- The developer may edit only name, email, photo, designation and notification choices. Anything else is ignored.
- Email must be valid and cannot be blanked on this account type: "Email is required for this account".

---

###### Flow 6 — Relationship Manager card

- **Actor:** A signed-in developer.

1. On My Account, the **Your Relationship Manager** card shows: "Your dedicated Keydemand point of contact", the manager's name and designation, a **Call** button with the number, and an **Email** button.
2. If no manager is assigned yet: "Your relationship manager will be assigned shortly" with the support email.
3. The card stays empty if the assigned manager has left or been deactivated.
4. The developer does **not** get a "Request help" button. That is for enterprise brands only.

**How a manager is assigned:** Keydemand assigns an Account Handler to the developer or to the developer's company in the Control Panel.

---

###### Flow 7 — How Keydemand creates the developer's projects (summary)

- **Actor:** A Keydemand member with project permission.
- **Prerequisites:** An approved, active developer account. Full steps are in the Control Panel guide.

1. The member opens **Listing Management → Projects** and chooses **Add project** for the developer. The developer **cannot** do this. The web app's own project form is retired.
2. The shared **Project form** collects the fields below. Every starred field is required.
3. The project is saved under the developer. A project that names a developer who is not live is refused.
4. The project is **public by default**. The member may restrict the audience.
5. Large brochure files are compressed automatically after upload.

**Project form fields (developer)**

| Field | Required |
| :---- | :---: |
| Asset class and transaction type | Yes |
| City and Location (picked from the map list) | Yes |
| Project Name | Yes |
| Project Type: IT Parks, Mixed Use, Office Building, Mall, Highstreet | Yes |
| Total Project Size (sq. ft.), with carpet or built-up basis | Yes |
| Unit Size Min and Max (max cannot exceed total size) | Yes |
| Efficiency (%) (above 0 and up to 100) | Yes |
| Project Status: Ready to Move or Under Construction | Yes |
| Possession month and year (or not applicable) | Yes |
| About Project | Yes |
| OC Status: Received, Applied, Not Available, Under Construction | Yes |
| Features and Amenities (at least one) | Yes |
| Images and Videos (at least one image or a video) | Yes |
| Google Maps Link or pin | Yes |
| Brochure, floor plans, documents | No |
| Assigned Keydemand contact | No |

**Matching and leads from a project**

- A project is relevant to a demand when the class fits, the transaction matches, the city matches, the demand's size fits the project's unit range (10% below the smallest to 20% above the largest) and the project is within 3 km of a requested location.
- **Which demands a project serves:** Office projects serve Office demands. Retail, F&B and Highstreet projects serve Retail and F&B demands. Mixed Use serves both. A project never serves Managed Space demands.
- When a brand, tenant or agent presses **Show Interest** (or a visitor sends an enquiry), a lead goes to the **project's Keydemand Relationship Manager** and a notification goes to the developer (Flow 8).
- Keydemand staff see "Project Leads received" for every project.

---

###### Flow 8 — Interest in the developer's project

- **Actor:** The system, then the developer and Keydemand.
- **Prerequisites:** Someone shows interest in a project.

1. A registered user taps **Show Interest**, or a visitor submits a short enquiry. Details sent: name, user type, mobile number, city and email when given.
2. The lead is recorded and sent to the project's Keydemand Relationship Manager and super admin.
3. The developer is notified of the **Project interest received**: in-app, push, WhatsApp and email.
4. Because developers cannot open the app beyond My Account, **email is the channel that actually reaches them**. The in-app row and its link are unreachable.
5. Keydemand follows up with the lead and tells the developer by phone or email.

---

###### Flow 9 — Deactivation, deletion and removal

- **Actor:** Keydemand.
- A developer **cannot** deactivate or delete their own account. Those routes are blocked by the lockdown.
- Keydemand deactivates, reactivates or deletes the developer in the Control Panel. A deactivation takes the developer's active projects down. A deletion removes the projects. The Control Panel reports how many were affected.
- Keydemand can also change the developer's mobile number (the number is their sign-in identity and must be unique).

---

###### Flow 10 — Sign out

1. Use **Logout** from the profile menu or My Account.
2. The session ends. Signing out and refreshing a session are allowed even under the lockdown.

---

##### 4. Notifications a Developer Receives

| Event | When | Channels |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Welcome | The account is first created through registration | In-app, WhatsApp, email |
| Project interest received | Someone shows interest in the developer's project | In-app, push, WhatsApp, email (email is the one that lands) |
| Daily summary (6 pm India time) | Once a day if anything applies | Push, WhatsApp |

Notes:

- The in-app notification centre is not reachable for developers, so in-app rows are never seen.
- The "Profile incomplete" reminder applies only to people who start a registration. The List your project form creates no such record.
- Keydemand receives its own alerts: an operations email for each new developer enquiry, and in-app and email alerts for project leads.

---

##### 5. Limits and Rules

| Rule | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Free demands, listings or reveals | None. All blocked |
| One-time code | 6 digits |
| Pages a signed-in developer can open | My Account only |
| Fields a developer can edit | Name, email, photo, designation, notification choices |
| Mobile number change | Keydemand only |
| Lead statuses | New, Contacted, Closed, Converted |
| Repeat submission while a lead is open | Updates the lead, no duplicate |
| Name and company length | 150 characters |
| GST or CIN | 15-character GSTIN or 21-character CIN, optional |
| Approval time promised on screen | 24 hours |
| Project match distance | 3 km |
| Project unit-size window | 10% below the smallest to 20% above the largest |

---

##### 6. Coverage Checklist

###### Web routes covered

| Route area | Covered in |
| :---- | :---- |
| List your project (page and pop-up) | Flow 1 |
| Sign-in, verify code, role (hidden), register (developer form) | Flows 1, 4 |
| My Account | Flows 5, 6 |
| Information pages (Contact, About, FAQs, Privacy, Terms, Cookie settings) | Section 2 |
| Projects (staff-created) | Flows 7, 8 |
| Dashboard, Saved, Notifications, Search, Properties, Demands, Leads, Subscription, Profile, Delete Account | Blocked for this persona (Section 2) |

###### Core service areas covered

Auth (sign-in, approval gate), Users (own profile), Leads (onboarding, project interest), Projects (staff-created), Notifications, Assistance (not available to developers), plus the RM-only lockdown in the access layer.

Request a new code."; too soon "Please wait N seconds before requesting another OTP." (countdown). _(§ 3 Flow 1 › Edge cases)_

### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Approval/rejection wording conflicts: the app shows "Approved within 24 hours" while the wording library says "Your Keydemand team access is awaiting approval."; same for the not-approved message.
- Developer notifications (in-app, push, WhatsApp, Daily summary push/WhatsApp) are listed as sent but the persona cannot open the app beyond My Account; push/WhatsApp delivery to developers is not confirmed, only "email is the one that lands".
- Daily summary is listed for developers although they have nothing (no demands, matches) to summarise; trigger "if anything applies" is undefined.
- Welcome is sent only when "account first created through registration", but developers never register themselves (accounts are created by Keydemand); applicability of Welcome is unclear.
- The "notification choices" are editable by developers although the notification centre is unreachable.
- Profile is hidden from the menu yet My Account allows profile editing.
- Flow 1 prerequisite "an approved developer account exists" vs the form being guests-only in the menu.
- Signing in before an account exists shows a role picker without the Developer card; no guidance for the in-progress developer beyond the legacy message.
- Project form says "the web app's own project form is retired" and "Full steps are in the Control Panel guide"; the project form fields here may be incomplete versus that guide.
- Project "public by default" while the developer sees nothing; no stated way to see what audience is set.

##### 1. Persona snapshot

| Aspect | Detail |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Who** | Keydemand employees who work the marketplace day to day: relationship managers, account handlers and sales and operations staff. |
| **Goals** | Look after enterprise brands and tenants, work high-value leads, follow developer projects, post supply and demand on behalf of customers, manage the broker network, and answer inbound leads. |
| **How onboarded** | Created by a Control Panel administrator. They never sign up themselves. They then sign in to the user app with phone number and a one-time code, like every other user. |
| **Identity** | A staff member can hold **two** logins: a user-app login (this file) and a separate Control Panel login with email and password. The two share nothing. |
| **Sub-roles** | **Keydemand Agent** and **BRM** (broker relationship manager). BRM has everything an agent has, plus broker management. |
| **Asset-class scope** | All four: Retail, F&B, Office, Managed Space. |

###### What the team can do in the user app

- **Run a desk.** A staff dashboard with tabs for properties, demands, projects, enterprise accounts, high-value leads, inbound leads and (for BRMs) agents.
- **Explore demands.** The only persona that can browse the demand marketplace, if the "Explore Demand" switch is on.
- **Post** properties and demands, with no free limit and no subscription.
- **Reveal contact numbers** for free and instantly.
- **Look after enterprise accounts** assigned to them, including their demands and "request help from my RM" queue.
- **Answer enquiries** across Keydemand-held inventory.

###### What the team cannot do in the user app

| Blocked action | Why |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Buy a subscription** | Subscriptions are for agents. Staff do not need one. |
| **Deactivate or delete their own account** | Staff accounts are managed by Keydemand. The profile shows "Your account is managed by Keydemand. To deactivate or delete it, contact the Keydemand team." |
| **Edit other people's listings** | In the user app a member can edit, deactivate or delete only **their own properties**, and demands only for accounts on whose team they sit. Everything else goes through the Control Panel. |
| **Approve or reject listings, change prices, manage users, bulk upload, set high-value rules** | Control Panel functions. |
| **Create projects or centres in the web app** | The web app's "Add Centre" is retired. Projects are made in the Control Panel. |
| **Use features whose switch is off** | Each member has switches, set by an administrator (see below). |

###### The permission switches

An administrator controls what each staff member sees. Two are always on. The rest follow the member's sub-role template unless a custom set is saved for that member.

| Switch | What it opens | Always on? |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Dashboard** | The staff dashboard | Yes |
| **Explore Property** | Property search | Yes |
| **Explore Demand** | Demand search, other posters' demand pages, relevant-demand rails | No |
| **Post Property** | The post property form (also gates posting a project record) | No |
| **Post Demand** | The post demand form | No |
| **Broker Management** | The Property Agents tab | BRM only (by template) |
| **My Listings** | Own properties and demands tab | No |
| **KD Listings** | Team-wide properties and demands | No |
| **Assigned Brands** | Enterprise accounts assigned to the member, and their help requests | No |
| **KD Brands** | All enterprise accounts, and all help requests | No |
| **Tagged Projects** | Projects tagged to the member | No |
| **All Projects** | All projects | No |
| **High Value Leads** | The high-value lead register | No |
| **Notifications and Enquiries** | Leads, enquiries, notification centre and saved items on the desk | No |

**Templates:** Keydemand Agent gets every switch except Broker Management. BRM gets all of them. A member with a custom set gets exactly that set (plus the two always-on switches).

##### 2. Screen and navigation map

###### Menu items a staff member sees

| Menu item | Where it goes | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Home** | Landing page | Always |
| **Explore Properties** | Search | Needs Explore Property (always on) |
| **Projects** | Search, projects view | Always |
| **Explore Demands** | Search, demands view | Staff only, and needs Explore Demand |
| **Post Property** | Property form | Needs Post Property |
| **Post Demand** | Demand form | Needs Post Demand |
| **Dashboard** | The staff dashboard | Always |
| **Leads** | Inbound lead register | Staff only |
| **Profile** | Profile and preferences | Always |
| **Saved** | Favourites | Always |
| **Notifications** | Notification centre | Always |

**Not shown to staff:** Subscription and Agent Subscription (agents only). Relationship Manager card (enterprise accounts only).

###### After signing in

A staff member who signs in with no return address lands on the **dashboard**. Everyone else lands on the home page. A shared listing link still wins for staff, so they land on that listing.

###### The staff dashboard

| Tab | What it shows | Scope choices | Switch needed |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Overview** | Headline tiles for the member's book | My and KD splits, Assigned and All splits | Dashboard |
| **Properties** | Properties with per-card match counts and lead counts. Search by ID, title or location. | **Self** (own) or **KD** (team) | My Listings, KD Listings |
| **Demands** | Requirements filed. A card has no photo and shows the size instead. | **Self**, **KD** or **My brands** | My Listings, KD Listings |
| **Projects** | Developments tagged to the member, with enquiry drill-down. Filter by city, status (active, inactive, archived, all) and category (standard, premium, exclusive). | **Assigned** or **All** | Tagged Projects, All Projects |
| **Enterprise** | The brands and tenants the member handles. Filter by type (brand, office tenant, managed-space occupier) and city. | **Assigned** or **All** | Assigned Brands, KD Brands |
| **High Value Leads** | Rules routed to the member, and the requirements inside them, including leads matched by no rule | **Assigned** or **All** | High Value Leads |
| **Leads** | Inbound lead register with source cards | Assigned to me, Callbacks, Enterprise, Project interest, Managed office, Developers, Operators | Notifications and Enquiries |
| **Property Agents** | The external broker roster | All agents | Broker Management |
| **Help requests** | "Request help from my RM" queue (shown for enterprise handlers) | Assigned or All | Assigned Brands, KD Brands |

###### Mobile versus desktop

The same menu list drives the pill bar, the profile dropdown, the phone drawer and the bottom bar. On a phone the bottom bar carries Home, Explore, Menu and Profile, and the drawer carries the desk items. On iOS nothing changes for staff, since they never see purchase screens.

---

##### 3. End-to-end flows

###### Flow 1 — Onboarding, first login and session

- **Actor:** New staff member, and a Control Panel administrator.
- **Prerequisites:** An administrator has created the staff account and assigned a sub-role.

1. An administrator creates the member in the Control Panel and sets their sub-role and switches. (See [Control Panel flows](../admin-panel/02-functional-flows.md).)
2. The member opens the web or mobile app and signs in with their phone number and a 6-digit code. There is no role-selection step, because the number is already known.
3. They tick the consent box (over 18, Terms and Privacy).
4. They land on the **dashboard**.
5. Staff do not receive a welcome message or a "profile incomplete" nudge under the latest notification rules (see Section 4).
6. The session refreshes quietly while they work. Logging out forgets the device for push alerts.

**Refusals:** an inactive or removed member is refused sign-in or refresh. A member whose rights were removed loses them at once, because the current state is checked on every call, not the state at sign-in.

**Edge cases**

- A member whose switch is turned off sees the matching menu item vanish. If they open its address directly they are sent to the dashboard.
- Changing a sub-role template changes every member who follows it, with no re-login.

###### Flow 2 — Profile and preferences

- **Actor:** Staff member.

1. Open **Profile**, then **Edit Profile**.
2. **Editable:** name, email, profile picture, designation, assigned regions, and the three notification switches (push, WhatsApp, email).
3. **Not editable:** phone number, sub-role, switches. An administrator manages those.
4. **Rules:** a designation needs at least one letter. An email must be real (valid, not a disposable domain, with a mail server).
5. Unsaved changes prompt "Discard your changes?". Saving prompts "Save these changes?".

**Edge cases:** there is no Deactivate or Delete Account for staff. The profile shows the "managed by Keydemand" message instead.

###### Flow 3 — Explore properties and projects

- **Actor:** Staff member.

1. Open Explore Properties. Photos are always visible to staff.
2. Filter by city, asset class, lease or buy, locality and class ranges. Search by listing ID or an old v1 number.
3. Open any property. Staff see all hidden photos and the real owner.
4. Project search and detail work as for other users.

**Edge cases:** staff see every property regardless of its "Who can see this" setting. A listing posted by a staff member shows as "Posted by Keydemand" to everyone else, and its revealed contact reads "Keydemand" with the phone number shown but no personal email or company.

###### Flow 4 — Explore demands

- **Actor:** Staff member with **Explore Demand** on.
- **Prerequisites:** The switch is on.

1. Open **Explore Demands**. The search is pinned to demands.
2. Filter and open a demand. Staff see the full requirement and the poster.
3. A demand held by Keydemand for a brand shows as the brand.
4. Without the switch, the menu item is hidden, the search refuses demands, other posters' demand pages are refused, and relevant-demand rails are hidden. There is one exception: a member who holds the High Value Leads switch can open a demand that has a live high-value lead.

**System side-effects:** none. Reading is free.

###### Flow 5 — Post a property

- **Actor:** Staff member with **Post Property** on.

1. Open **Post Property**.
2. Fill the shared form. The fields are the same as for agents
3. **Choose who can see it.** This control is **only** for staff posts. At least one audience must be ticked, otherwise the form is refused. Options: Everyone, Office Tenant, Enterprise Tenant, Retail Brand, F&B Brand, Enterprise Brand, Keydemand, Agent. Choosing Everyone stores it alone.
4. Optionally tick **hide from agents.**
5. Submit.

**Differences from an agent post**

| Aspect | Staff | Agent |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Free limit | None | 1 shared free listing |
| Subscription coverage | Not needed | Needed once subscribed |
| Asset classes | All four, including Managed Space | The agent's registered classes |
| Audience control | Yes | No (open to everyone) |

**System side-effects:** "Property posted" message on WhatsApp, email (with the property PDF attached) and in-app, plus a "Property posted successfully" toast. Matching starts.

**Edge cases**

- In production, whether a staff post still waits for approval depends on the same rule as other posts **(inferred)**. Test environments approve at once.
- Control Panel posting on behalf of an agent or customer uses a separate form and is not described here.

###### Flow 6 — Post a demand (for self or a customer)

- **Actor:** Staff member with **Post Demand** on.

1. Open **Post Demand**. The shared form opens. If the member is handling an enterprise brand, saved **Formats** (templates) can pre-fill it.
2. Choose the demand audience. Only staff choose it. Options: Developer, Keydemand team, Agent. At least one must be ticked.
3. Fill the requirement and submit.
4. A requirement filed for a brand through a Format is shown to everyone as **the brand**, while permissions still follow the staff member.
5. Large requirements in major cities are routed to the high-value register ([Flow 11](#flow-11--high-value-leads)). Agent-posted demands are exempt from this.

**System side-effects:** "Demand posted" message in-app and as a toast. Leads and contact views on a brand demand held by staff go to the member **and** every active user of that brand.

###### Flow 7 — Edit, deactivate or delete listings

- **Actor:** Staff member.

1. **Own properties:** edit, deactivate, activate or delete from the property page or dashboard, exactly as an agent would.
2. **Demands:** allowed when the staff member is on the account's Keydemand team. The team is the account's relationship manager, any members added to its team, and the company's team. For an enterprise tenant, the team is the poster's point of contact and the company's team.
3. **Enterprise accounts:** users of the same enterprise brand or tenant company can manage all of that account's demands, including colleagues' and those Keydemand filed.
4. **Anything else** (agents' listings, other accounts' demands, colleagues' unlinked properties) is refused with a message that the edit must go through the Control Panel.

**Edge cases:** the right is recalculated each time. A member removed from the team, or a brand demoted to individual, loses it immediately.

###### Flow 8 — Reveal a contact number

- **Actor:** Staff member.

1. Tap **View number** on a property or demand.
2. The number is revealed at once, free and uncounted, even for a brand demand that would need an approval from other users.
3. The owner is told their number was viewed. A staff owner is told straight away on WhatsApp, in-app and as a toast, for their own properties and demands and for demands of enterprise accounts assigned to them (see Section 4).

**Edge cases:** a listing that is no longer live is refused for everyone except staff.

###### Flow 9 — Enquiries, requests and image requests

- **Actor:** Staff member.

1. **Send:** staff can send enquiries and image requests like other users.
2. **Receive and answer:** requests on staff-owned listings appear under Dashboard and Leads. Accept or reject. Image requests are answered the same way as for agents.
3. **Browse everything:** with the Notifications and Enquiries switch, staff can see enquiries across Keydemand-held inventory.
4. A request expires after 72 hours without an answer. The sender is told if the listing ends first.

###### Flow 10 — Work the inbound leads register

- **Actor:** Staff member with **Notifications and Enquiries** on.

1. Open **Leads**. Summary cards count leads by status and by source.
2. Filter by status (New, Contacted, Converted, Closed), by source and by city.
3. Source options: **Assigned to me**, **Callbacks** (the home-page request), **Enterprise** (Enterprise Solution form), **Project interest**, **Managed office**, **Developers** and **Operators** (the "List your project" intake).
4. Read each row and contact the lead by phone.
5. **Updating status, assigning and converting a lead** happens in the Control Panel, not in this view. The user-app register is read-only **(verified in the page: no edit controls)**.

**System side-effects:** none from reading. A project-interest lead alerts the project's developer contact and only the staff members assigned to that project, on WhatsApp, email and in-app. Leads assigned to the member from the Control Panel, and new developer, operator and enterprise enquiries, are also notified on WhatsApp, email and in-app (see Section 4).

###### Flow 11 — High-value leads

- **Actor:** Staff member with **High Value Leads** on.

1. Open the **High Value Leads** tab. Choose **Assigned** or **All**.
2. The tab groups leads by rule (city, asset class, size). A group called "direct" holds leads that matched no rule.
3. Open a lead and tap **View Requirement.** This reveals the poster's mobile number and records who viewed it.
4. Contact the poster and service the requirement.
5. **Unlocking a lead to agents, assigning it and editing rules happen in the Control Panel. When a high-value lead is assigned to the member, they are notified on WhatsApp, email and in-app (see Section 4).**

**How a lead appears:** a requirement posted by a brand or tenant (not an agent) in one of eight major cities, above the rule's minimum size, is hidden from agents and filed as a lead.

###### Flow 12 — Enterprise accounts and "Request help from my RM"

- **Actor:** Relationship manager or team member.

1. Open **Enterprise**. Choose **Assigned** (accounts where the member is the point of contact or on the team) or **All** (needs KD Brands).
2. Open an account to see its demands and format specifications, and the leads they received or the properties they contacted.
3. Open **Help requests.** Each request names the account, the action asked for (for example deactivate a demand, or another request) and an optional note.
4. Do the work, or contact the account. Then tap **Mark resolved.** The requester gets "Marked resolved. The requester has been notified."

**How requests arrive:** an enterprise user taps "Request help from my RM". If the account has an active relationship manager, that person gets an in-app, email and WhatsApp alert, and other team members get an in-app row. With no active manager, the operations inbox gets the email instead.

**Edge cases:** the queue is scoped to accounts the member is on, and recalculated from the current team, so a reassigned account moves queues at once.

###### Flow 13 — Projects and operators

- **Actor:** Staff member with **Tagged Projects** or **All Projects.**

1. Open **Projects.** Choose **Assigned** or **All.**
2. Open a project to see the enquiries received, split into interest and enquiry.
3. The project page and PDF work as for other users.
4. **Creating or editing projects and centres is done in the Control Panel. The member is notified in-app when a project is assigned to them and when an assigned project receives a relevant demand (see Section 4).** A lookup of operators exists for staff who hold **Post Property**, to attach a centre to an operator, but the web form that used it is retired.

###### Flow 14 — Broker management (BRM)

- **Actor:** BRM with **Broker Management** on.

1. Open **Property Agents.** The roster can be sorted by most properties, most demands, most leads, most enquiries or most recent.
2. Open an agent to see activity: listings, demands, leads and enquiries.
3. Open **subscription** to see the agent's plan history and invoices.
4. This view is **read-only.** Granting plans and changing prices are Control Panel functions.

###### Flow 15 — Notifications centre, saved items and search

- **Actor:** Staff member.

1. **Notifications:** the bell and the page work as for agents, with the same read and mark-all actions. A separate desk view lists the member's own notification centre.
2. **Saved:** favourites of properties and projects.
3. **Search:** staff search properties, projects **and demands** (with Explore Demand on).

###### Flow 16 — Relationship manager card and account handover

- **Actor:** Enterprise customer, staff member and administrator.

1. An enterprise brand or tenant sees a **Relationship Manager** card with the assigned staff member's name and phone, and a Call button. The card appears only while that member is active. Once the member is deactivated or removed, the card stops showing them.
2. An administrator can assign a staff member as the point of contact, or add them to an account's team. The member is alerted by email, with the user's brand, user type, asset class, name, phone number and city, and in-app ("New enterprise user assigned").
3. **Before a staff member leaves**, their book (listings, accounts, assignments) is either moved straight to another member or **held** by an administrator for later reassignment. Deactivating a member is blocked until this is done.

###### Flow 17 — Help, grievance and account removal

- **Actor:** Staff member.

1. Help content: Contact page, FAQs and the notification page's Help Desk link.
2. Staff cannot deactivate or delete their account. They ask a Control Panel administrator.

##### 4. Notifications

**Channel key:** WhatsApp and Email are sent outside the app. In-app = notification centre. Toast = short on-screen message shown in the app at the moment of the action. Attachment = file sent with the message. CTA = the button on the message. NA = not sent on that channel. Text in square brackets is filled in when the message is sent. Messages go out as the event happens; there is no daily digest for staff.

| Event | When it fires | WhatsApp | Email | In-app notification | Toast | Attachment | CTA |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **New enterprise user assigned** | A new enterprise user is assigned to the member as point of contact | NA | Hi [name], A new enterprise user has been assigned to you: [brand name], [user type], [asset class], [user name], [phone number], [city]. View details. | A new [brand name] is assigned to you, view details. | NA | NA | View Details |
| **New project assigned** | A new project is assigned to the member as point of contact | NA | NA | A new project [ID] is assigned to you, view details. | NA | NA | NA |
| **Assigned project lead** | A new lead comes in on a project assigned to the member. Sent only to the assigned staff members. | Hi [Name], you have a new lead on [Project name] in [City] from [User type]. The full details are on the project page. | Subject: New lead on [Project name] — Hi [Name], — A new lead has come in on [Project name], [City]. — Name: [Name]; Type: [User type]; City: [City]; Received: [Date] — Full details are on the project page. | New lead on [Project name] from [User type], [City]. Tap to view the details. | NA | NA | View Lead |
| **Relevant demand to assigned project** | A project assigned to the member receives a new relevant demand | NA | NA | [Project name], [City] has received relevant demand [ID]. | NA | NA | NA |
| **Property posted by self** | The member posts a property | Hi [Name], your [property type] property [property ID] at [Locality], [City] is now live on Keydemand. Tap below to view your listing and share it with potential occupiers. | Subject: Your property [Property ID] is live on Keydemand — Hi [Name], — Your [property type] property [Property ID] at [Locality], [City] has been posted successfully and is now live. — The listing sheet is attached. | [Type] property [ID] in [Locality], [City] is live. Download attached PDF. | Property posted successfully | Property PDF | View property |
| **Demand posted by self** | The member posts a demand | NA | NA | Requirement [ID] for [Type] in [Locality], [City] is live. | Requirement [ID] for [Type] in [Locality], [City] is live. | NA | NA |
| **Relevant property for own demand** | A new property matches a requirement the member posted | [40] new properties match your requirements. Explore them now. | NA | A property matches your requirement in [Locality], [City]. Tap to view. | New match for your requirement in [Locality]. | NA | View relevancy |
| **Relevant property for assigned enterprise demand** | A new property matches a requirement of an enterprise account assigned to the member | NA | Hi [name], Your brands [brand name] [relevancy], [brand name] [relevancy], [brand name] [relevancy], [brand name] [relevancy], [brand name] [relevancy] etc. have new relevant properties. Kindly check if any property interests you. | [Brand name] has received a relevant property [ID] in [Locality], [City]. | NA | NA | View demand |
| **Relevant demand for own property** | A new requirement matches a property the member listed | [40] new requirements match your listings. Explore them now. | NA | A requirement matches your property in [Locality], [City]. Tap to view. | New demand matches your property in [Locality]. | NA | View Relevancy |
| **My phone number viewed** | Someone views the member's number on their own property or demand, or on an assigned enterprise account's demand | [User type] [User name] viewed your number for property [ID] in [Locality]. | NA | [User type] [User name] viewed your number for property [ID] in [Locality]. | [User type] [User name] viewed your number for property [ID] in [Locality]. | NA | View phone number |
| **Image request received** | Someone asks to view the hidden images of a property the member uploaded | Hi [Name], [User type] is interested in your property at [Locality], [City] and has requested to view images. Kindly action the request. | NA | [User type] is interested in your [property type] [property ID] at [Locality], [City] and has requested to view images. Kindly action the request. | NA | NA | Review Request |
| **Image request answered** | The owner answers an image request the member sent | Approved: Hi [Name], the images you requested for the property at [Locality], [City] on Keydemand are now available. View them now. — Declined: Hi [Name], your image request for the property at [Locality], [City] was not approved. Keep exploring other matching properties. | NA | Approved: Images are now available for the property at [Locality], [City] that you requested. View them now. — Declined: Image request done by you for [property type] [property ID] is rejected. | NA | NA | View Property |
| **New marketing lead: developer** | A new developer enquiry is received | Developer enquiry form details | Developer enquiry form details | A new developer enquiry is done by [developer name], [user name]. | NA | NA | View Lead |
| **New marketing lead: operator** | A new operator enquiry is received | Operator enquiry form details | Operator enquiry form details | A new operator enquiry is done by [operator name], [user name]. | NA | NA | View Lead |
| **New marketing lead: enterprise** | A new enterprise enquiry, either fresh or from an individual who taps Become an enterprise | Brand name, mobile number, name of the person, date, email ID (if provided) | Brand name, mobile number, name of the person, date, email ID (if provided) | A new enterprise enquiry is done by [brand name]. | NA | NA | View Lead |
| **Lead assigned to me** | The Control Panel assigns a lead to the member | Assigned lead details | Assigned lead details | Unchanged: the current in-app message | NA | NA | View Lead |
| **High-value lead assigned to me** | The Control Panel assigns a high-value lead to the member | Assigned high-value lead details | Assigned high-value lead details | Unchanged: the current in-app message | NA | NA | View Lead |

**No longer sent to staff under the latest rules:** welcome, profile incomplete, receipts for editing, deactivating or deleting a property or demand, help requested by an enterprise brand, request closed (listing unavailable), new demands in your city, listing is 90 days old, and the 6 pm daily summary.

**Not sent to staff:** contact request received (brands), contact request answered (agents), all subscription messages (agents), upsell prompts and free-limit notices (agents, brands, occupiers).

---

##### 5. Limits and rules

| Rule | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Free listings | None. Staff post without limit. |
| Contact reveals | Free and unlimited |
| Subscription | Not applicable |
| Asset classes | All four |
| Visibility of properties | All, ignoring the "Who can see this" setting |
| Property audience (staff posts) | Required. At least one box ticked. |
| Demand audience (staff posts) | Required. Developer, Keydemand team, Agent. At least one ticked. |
| Who can edit a listing | Own properties. Demands only for accounts on the member's team. |
| Self-deactivate or delete | Not allowed |
| Switches | 14, with two always on |
| Sub-roles | Keydemand Agent, BRM |
| Request expiry | 72 hours |
| One-time code | 6 digits, 30-second resend gap, at most 3 sends in 5 minutes |
| Staff identity on revealed contacts | Others see "Keydemand" plus the phone number, with no email or company |
| Messaging for enterprise accounts | In-app and push only. No WhatsApp or email to enterprise users. |

---

##### 6. Coverage checklist

**Web app routes covered:** Sign-in (Phone, Verify, Success), Home, Search and Explore Properties, Explore Demands (search view), Property detail, Property post, Property edit, Demand post, Demand edit, Demand detail, Project detail, Project enquiries, Dashboard (all staff tabs), Leads, Profile, Profile edit, Saved, Notifications, Account, Contact, FAQs, Menu, the redirect for old Demands and Agents addresses.

**Core API areas covered:** the staff desk (dashboard, listings, projects, project enquiries, leads, enquiries, notifications, saved, operators, brokers and broker subscription, high-value register and view, enterprise accounts and their leads, help-request queue and resolve), auth, users, properties, demands, enquiries, contact unlock, notifications, search, leads, assistance, relationship manager card.

**Not covered here (Control Panel):** moderation, user and staff management, role and switch editing, pricing, subscriptions, bulk upload, high-value rule setup and unlock, lead assignment and conversion, V1 completion, insights, observability. See the [Control Panel flows](../admin-panel/02-functional-flows.md).

### Business rules extracted
- **BR-PD-1431** — Keydemand Team personas are employees: relationship managers, account handlers, sales and operations staff. _(§ 1. Persona snapshot)_
- **BR-PD-1432** — Staff are created by a Control Panel administrator and never sign up themselves; they then sign in to the user app with phone number and one-time code. _(§ 1)_
- **BR-PD-1433** — A staff member can hold two separate logins: user-app (phone + code) and Control Panel (email + password); the two share nothing. _(§ 1)_
- **BR-PD-1434** — Sub-roles are Keydemand Agent and BRM (broker relationship manager); BRM has everything an agent has plus broker management. _(§ 1)_
- **BR-PD-1435** — Asset-class scope for staff: Retail, F&B, Office, Managed Space (all four). _(§ 1)_
- **BR-PD-1436** — Staff can run a desk dashboard with tabs for properties, demands, projects, enterprise accounts, high-value leads, inbound leads and (BRMs) agents. _(§ 1 › What the team can do)_
- **BR-PD-1437** — Staff are the only persona that can browse the demand marketplace, if the "Explore Demand" switch is on. _(§ 1 › What the team can do)_
- **BR-PD-1438** — Staff post properties and demands with no free limit and no subscription. _(§ 1 › What the team can do)_
- **BR-PD-1439** — Staff reveal contact numbers for free and instantly. _(§ 1 › What the team can do)_
- **BR-PD-1440** — Staff look after enterprise accounts assigned to them, including their demands and the "request help from my RM" queue. _(§ 1 › What the team can do)_
- **BR-PD-1441** — Staff cannot buy a subscription (subscriptions are for agents). _(§ 1 › cannot)_
- **BR-PD-1442** — Staff cannot deactivate or delete their own account; profile shows "Your account is managed by Keydemand. To deactivate or delete it, contact the Keydemand team." _(§ 1 › cannot)_
- **BR-PD-1443** — In the user app a staff member can edit, deactivate or delete only their own properties, and demands only for accounts on whose team they sit; everything else goes through the Control Panel. _(§ 1 › cannot)_
- **BR-PD-1444** — Approving/rejecting listings, changing prices, managing users, bulk upload and setting high-value rules are Control Panel functions, not user app. _(§ 1 › cannot)_
- **BR-PD-1445** — Staff cannot create projects or centres in the web app; "Add Centre" is retired and projects are made in the Control Panel. _(§ 1 › cannot)_
- **BR-PD-1446** — Staff cannot use features whose switch is off; switches are set by an administrator per member. _(§ 1 › cannot)_
- **BR-PD-1447** — Dashboard and Explore Property switches are always on; the rest follow the member's sub-role template unless a custom set is saved. _(§ 1 › permission switches)_

- **BR-PD-1450** — Switch "Post Demand" opens the post demand form; not always on. _(§ 1 › switches)_
- **BR-PD-1451** — Switch "Broker Management" opens the Property Agents tab; BRM only (by template). _(§ 1 › switches)_
- **BR-PD-1452** — Switch "My Listings" opens own properties and demands tab; "KD Listings" opens team-wide properties and demands; neither always on. _(§ 1 › switches)_

- **BR-PD-1454** — Switch "Tagged Projects" opens projects tagged to the member; "All Projects" opens all projects. _(§ 1 › switches)_

### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Contents lists "7. Open questions / gaps / not built" and "8. Source appendix", but the doc has only up to "7. Source appendix"; the open-questions section is missing.
- Flow 5: whether a staff post waits for approval in production is marked "(inferred)".
- Flow 5 step 2 text ends without a full stop/explicit field list ("The fields are the same as for agents").
- The business-rules source `docs/businessrules/Keydemand Team 30062026 - Final.docx.md` was listed but not read; flows come from code only.
- Control Panel posting on behalf of an agent or customer is "not described here".
- Several notifications use "Unchanged: the current in-app message" (Lead assigned to me, High-value lead assigned) without stating the text; WhatsApp/email "details" content is unspecified for developer, operator, enterprise and assigned leads.
- Flow 1 says staff get no welcome/profile-incomplete, but staff are also stated to have no free limits etc.; the earlier "Flow 8" says the owner is told "straight away", while the Section 4 table lists "My phone number viewed" for staff owner only; behaviour for non-staff owners is not stated.
- "Switches: 14, with two always on" vs the list of 14 in the table: count matches, but BRM-only template for Broker Management is "by template" while a custom set may differ.
- Profile editing of "assigned regions" by staff conflicts with the statement that an administrator manages assignments (regions not explained).
- Section 2 says Projects menu item is "Always" shown, yet the Projects tab on the dashboard requires Tagged Projects / All Projects.
- "Explore Demands" is "Staff only" but the doc says an exception exists for High Value Leads holders without the switch (partial).
- Section 5 says enterprise messaging is "in-app and push only", while Flow 12 states an enterprise user's help request alerts the RM by email and WhatsApp (to staff, not enterprise); no contradiction but not clarified for enterprise tenants.
- Relevant property emails for assigned enterprise demands show repeated "[brand name] [relevancy]" up to five brands with "etc." with no rule for the cut-off.

##### 1\. Purpose and Who Uses It

**The Control Panel is Keydemand's internal operations console.** It is where staff create customer accounts, approve listings, route large leads, sell and adjust subscriptions, and watch the health of the platform. End customers never see it.

###### What It Is For

| Job | Where It Happens |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Onboard customers** who cannot self-register (developers, operators, enterprise brands and tenants) | User Management, Enterprise |
| **Run quality control** on new listings | Listing Management, Bulk Upload |
| **Post on behalf of customers** (properties, demands, projects, centres) | Listing Management |
| **Route high-value demands** to the Keydemand team | High Value Leads |
| **Handle inbound sales interest** and account deletion requests | Enquiries |
| **Sell and adjust subscriptions** | Subscription Management, agent pages |
| **Control who can sign up** by email domain | Email Domains |
| **Manage staff access** | Control Panel Users |
| **Watch the business and the system** | Dashboard, App Insights, Observability |
| **Finish migrated v1 data** | V1 Completion Queue |

###### Who Uses It

| Operator Type | Typical Person | What They Mostly Do |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Super Admin** | Tech lead, business head (two people in every environment) | Everything, including staff security and system settings |
| **Admin** | Operations manager | Customer, listing, subscription and lead operations; can manage staff except super admins |
| **Contributor** | Data-entry or content staff | Create and edit listings and projects, bulk upload, view users |
| **Business Viewer** | Leadership, finance | Dashboard and Business Insights, with export |
| **Tech Viewer** | Engineers, support | Technical Insights, with export |
| **Custom roles** | Anyone | Any mix of permissions a super admin or admin builds |

> **Two separate identities.** Control Panel operators sign in with an email and password. They are not customers and share no sign-in with the customer app. Keydemand team members who use the customer app (relationship managers and others) are managed from this panel but sign in there with phone and code.

---

##### 2\. Access Model

###### 2.1 Sign-In and Session Security

| Topic | How It Works |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Credentials** | Email and password. There is no self-registration. A super admin or admin creates the account. |
| **First sign-in** | New and reset accounts receive a one-time password by email. The first sign-in forces a password change, and there is no way to skip it. |
| **Password rules** | At least 6 characters, with one uppercase letter, one number and one special character. The form lists what is missing. |
| **Two-factor code** | When switched on for the environment, a 6-digit code is emailed after the password. It lasts 5 minutes and works once. **On in production.** |
| **Code limits** | 5 wrong codes void the code. Resend is allowed after 60 seconds, up to 3 times. At most 5 codes are issued per person in 15 minutes. |
| **Code delivery failure** | The sign-in fails with a "try again" message. The system never lets someone in because email failed. |
| **Password lockout** | 5 wrong passwords in a row lock the account for 15 minutes. It unlocks by itself, and a correct sign-in resets the count. |
| **Forgot password** | A 6-digit code is emailed (15 minutes). **Switched off in production**, where a super admin resets credentials instead. |
| **Session length** | Access lasts 30 minutes and renews quietly. A session left idle for 24 hours signs out. One in use stays signed in. |
| **Sign out** | Signs out this device. "Sign out everywhere" ends every session for the person. |
| **Instant revocation** | Disabling a person, changing their password, or changing their role or permissions takes effect on their next click. |
| **Stolen-session protection** | Reusing an old session token signs the person out everywhere and is logged. |
| **Security alert emails** | Sent to the person and to the DevOps group (UAT and production) for: sign-in from a new device or location, any super admin sign-in, 5 wrong passwords or codes, password changes and resets, and role or permission changes. |

###### 2.2 Operator Roles

| Role | What It Means | Who Can Change It |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Super Admin** | Every permission. Fixed set that cannot be edited. | Cannot be edited by anyone |
| **Admin** | Every permission except the two reserved for super admins (system settings and site-down). | Super admin only |
| **Contributor** | Create and edit listings and projects, bulk upload, formats, view users and dashboard. Cannot approve bulk uploads. | Super admin only |
| **Business Viewer** | Dashboard, Business Insights, export. Built in. | Super admin only |
| **Tech Viewer** | Technical Insights, export. Built in. Cannot change log levels. | Super admin only |
| **Custom** | Any selection of permissions. Built from the Control Panel Users screen. | Admin or super admin, within limits below |

###### 2.3 Staff Protection Rules

| Rule | Effect |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Only a super admin** may create a super admin, move anyone into or out of that role, disable or reset a super admin, or edit a built-in role | An admin who tries is refused, and the refusal is logged |
| **At most 2 active super admins** | A third cannot be created, promoted or re-enabled. Today the two are fixed in every environment. |
| **The last active super admin** cannot be disabled, deleted or demoted | Protects against lockout |
| **No self-escalation** | A non-super admin cannot give a role a permission they do not hold themselves |
| **Only a super admin can delete** an operator account | Admins can disable but not delete |
| **You cannot disable or delete yourself** | Prevents accidental lockout |
| **An operator holding a parked Keydemand hand-over cannot be deleted** | The work must be completed first |

###### 2.5 What Each Permission Gates

| Permission Area | Screens and Actions It Opens |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Users** | All user registers, user detail and edit pages, subscription grants on agents, Keydemand team management, hand-overs, KD role templates, enterprise conversion, POC assignment, account deletion requests, V1 profile queue |
| **Listings** | Property, demand and project detail, listing lists, moderation queue, edit, status change, delete, relevance panels, leads on a listing, PDF download, V1 property queue |
| **Projects** | Project register and detail, project create (developer and centre), edit, boosters, tag and untag units, delete and restore |
| **Bulk upload** | Templates, samples, upload, validation report, create for review, review queue, approve and reject |
| **Formats** | Add, edit and deactivate enterprise brand formats |
| **Subscription** | Cities tab (manage cities, regions, thresholds) and Price Management tab. Either permission opens the section. |
| **High-value leads** | Rules, city switches, lead register, assignment and release. Note: assigning a lead needs the "manage rules" permission, not the "unlock" one. |
| **Enquiries** | Marketing enquiries, listing leads, assignment, status |
| **Control Panel Users** | Staff list, create, edit, disable, reset, delete, roles, Email Domains |
| **App Insights** | Business views, Technical views, exports |
| **Observability** | Log levels and error digest settings |

###### 2.6 Keydemand Team Members (Customer-App Staff)

Keydemand team members are customer-app users that this panel manages. They are not Control Panel operators.

| Topic | How It Works |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Sub-roles** | Keydemand Agent and Business Relationship Manager (BRM). The BRM adds broker management. |
| **Role templates** | Each sub-role has a default set of customer-app permissions, editable on the Keydemand Team "Roles" screen. Changing a template changes everyone who follows it. |
| **Per-person overrides** | A member can carry their own permission set that replaces the template. "Reset to template" removes it. |
| **Always on** | Dashboard and Explore Property cannot be removed. |
| **The 14 toggles** | Dashboard, Explore Property, Explore Demand, Post Property, Post Demand, Broker Management, My Listings, KD Listings, Assigned Brands, KD Brands, Tagged Projects, All Projects, High Value Leads, Notifications and Enquiries. |
| **Enforced toggles** | Post Property, Post Demand and Explore Demand are actually enforced on the server. The others control what the app shows. |
| **Account teams** | Enterprise brands and tenants have a Point of Contact (POC) plus an optional Keydemand team. "RM", "Account Handler" and "POC" are the same role. |
| **Hand-over** | A member cannot be deactivated or deleted while they still hold accounts, listings, assignments or pending enquiries. The work is moved to another member, or parked with a Control Panel admin. See Flow 13 in the flows document. |

##### 4\. Module-by-Module Product Documentation

###### 4.1 Sign-In, Password and Session

**Purpose:** Let staff in safely, and stop others.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Email and password sign-in | Identify the operator | Email, password | Signed in, or code step if two-factor is on |
| Emailed sign-in code | Second factor in production | 6-digit code | Signed in. Wrong, expired and locked states show clear messages. |
| Resend code | Recover from a lost email | Resend button | New code after a 60-second wait, up to 3 times |
| Forced password change | Retire the emailed one-time password | First sign-in or after a reset | Cannot enter the console until a valid new password is set |
| Forgot password | Self-service recovery | Email, then emailed code and new password | All sessions end. **Off in production.** |
| Sign out and sign out everywhere | End sessions | Menu | Immediate revocation |
| Silent renewal | Avoid mid-task logouts | Automatic | Session extends while in use. 24-hour idle limit. |

**Validations and errors:** wrong credentials, disabled account, locked account (15 minutes), too many codes, expired code, weak password, email delivery failure, reset switched off.

###### 4.2 Dashboard

**Purpose:** A fast daily read on the business.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Primary outcomes** | Headline daily numbers | Open the page, choose Today, 7 days or 30 days | High-value leads, enterprise enquiries (split by persona), project leads and Keydemand team, each as "new in window" and "total" |
| **Secondary outcomes** | Deeper numbers | Expand the section | Subscriptions (active and expired), users by role, demands, properties and projects by asset class and poster type, leads, marketing enquiries, deleted properties, account deletions |
| **Per-member block** | Check one team member's work | Pick a Keydemand member | Enterprise accounts, high-value leads assigned, listings uploaded, projects assigned, leads |
| **Account and listing detail** | Register-level counts | Expand the detail block | Agents, tenants, developers and operators, Keydemand, enquiries and listings, with asset-class donuts |
| **Sidebar badges** | Show register sizes | Automatic | Counts beside the four account registers and Enterprise |

"Today" starts at midnight India time. The same numbers feed the daily admin email, so the screen and the email never disagree.

> **Indian mobile numbers on every create *(added, from 2026-10-30)*.** Customers sign in by SMS code, and codes go only to Indian mobiles (+91 followed by 10 digits starting 6 to 9). So that no account is created that can never sign in, the Control Panel applies the same rule when staff create an account, **before** the duplicate-phone check. It applies to: create Keydemand team member (replacing the looser international check), create agent, create tenant or occupier, add a member to a tenant account, create enterprise brand (primary user and each additional user), and add a user to an enterprise brand. Staff see "Enter a valid Indian mobile number (+91 followed by 10 digits starting 6-9)" with the field named. The form's phone box already adds +91, so only a number starting 0 to 5 is newly refused. Editing an existing account and bulk upload are unaffected. The allowed country codes are an environment setting (default India only).

###### Demands Keydemand holds for a brand *(added 2026-11-05)*

A **Keydemand-held brand demand** is a demand filed under a brand but posted by Keydemand: every migrated v1 brand demand, demands posted from the Control Panel on a brand's behalf (4.11), and Format-mode bulk uploads for brands.

**What changed (2026-11-03):** before, an agent who tapped "View number" saw the Keydemand member's own phone at once, and no lead was recorded. Now the tap sends a **contact request**, and no number is shown until someone answers it.

| Topic | How It Works |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Who can answer** | The poster, the brand's users, or the brand's Keydemand team (POC and team members). Any Keydemand member can also answer. The first answer wins; a second is refused. |
| **What is shared** | The accepter's contact. If the brand hides its name, a brand user is shared as phone only, under "Retail brand" or "F&B brand". |
| **Brand's own side** | The brand's users and its Keydemand team tapping the button on the brand's own demand get no request and no charge. |
| **Keydemand demand with no brand** | Unchanged. Immediate reveal. |
| **If nobody answers** | Reminder at 48 hours. The request expires at 72 hours and the viewer's free contact view is returned. |
| **Where it appears** | As a lead on the demand's Leads tab (4.10) and under Listing Leads (4.14). The Received tab now also lists requests addressed to the responders above, not only to the recipient. |
| **Back-fill (migration 129)** | Each earlier phone view on such a demand is recorded as an accepted contact-request lead, so lead history is complete. The viewer keeps the number they had and nothing is sent. Left out: views by Keydemand staff, the poster's own view, deleted viewers, deleted demands, and views that already have a request. The demand's lead total is unchanged. |

| **Bulk upload** | Load many listings | Upload a sheet | See Flow 22\. Sheets of demands (including enterprise Format mode), properties, developer projects and centres. Up to 5 MB, 2,000 rows and 120 columns. |

| **Validation report** | Fix before anything is created | Upload result | Row-by-row issues with cell reference, message and hint. Downloadable error report. |
| **Create for review, approve, reject** | Two-person control | Commit, then review | Rows are hidden until a reviewer approves them |

###### Acquisition & Sign-ups view *(added 2026-11-05)*

**Purpose:** Answer "where do visitors come from, how far do they get through sign-up, and where do they drop off". Read-only, same permission as the other Business views (App Insights, view Business), with the same CSV and Excel export.

| Part | What It Shows |
| :---- | :---- |
| **KPI strip** | Visitors landed, sign-ups opened, visit-to-sign-up rate, accounts registered, accounts registered from a campaign. No comparison with the previous period. |
| **Funnels** | Overall sign-up funnel: landed, opened sign-up, picked a role, code sent, code verified, saw the form, registered. Plus one funnel per persona, from the role screen on. Sign-ins of existing accounts are left out. |
| **Sources** | Where visitors arrive from: campaign tags (source, medium, campaign, content), referring websites, and Facebook / Instagram in-app browsers versus everything else. |
| **Drop-off** | Refusals people hit while signing up or in, by step, error code and the first field the error named. Counts requests, not people, so a retry counts again. |
| **Campaigns** | New accounts by the campaign source, campaign name and platform (website, Android, iOS) of their first visit, and campaign sign-ups by persona. |

- **Range limit:** the web-traffic parts (funnels, sources, drop-off) cover 7 days at most.
- **Privacy:** counts are distinct visitors; cells under 5 show as "<5".
- **Visit-to-sign-up is approximate**, because visitors come from web signals and accounts from the database.
- **Campaign and platform columns** fill only for accounts created after sign-up attribution was switched on. Older accounts show "not recorded" or "(none)".
- **Data source:** first-party web signals sent by the website and app, the API access logs, and the user records. Not Google Analytics.

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **First-party web signals** | Feed the Acquisition view without a third-party tool | The website and app send usage events to the platform | Events are logged and counted. Crawlers are ignored; over-limit or malformed events are dropped quietly. |
| **Sign-up attribution** | Know which campaign created an account | Saved at sign-up: first-touch campaign tags, platform, trigger | Stored on the new user and on marketing leads, only while the switch is on |
| **Two runtime switches** | Turn collection off without a deploy | Ops changes a setting in AWS Parameter Store | Takes effect within about 30 seconds. No Control Panel screen changes them. |

> **Operational additions *(added 2026-11-01)*:**
> - **Scheduled jobs are easier to diagnose.** A crashed job now writes a failure record. Jobs that carry on past failing items (daily digest, admin newsletter, incomplete-registration notices) are flagged "partial", and a new alarm, `scheduled-job-partial`, emails on production at one or more a day. Nothing about what the jobs do changed.
> - **Browser-error reports are clearer.** They name the endpoint with ids hidden and the error class, include the error page's reference, and no longer count a cancelled request as a network failure. This covers the Control Panel too.
> - **Privacy in provider logs.** Phone and email are masked in SMS, WhatsApp and email provider log lines.

###### 4.19 Notification Bell and Recent Activity

| Feature | Business Purpose | Trigger / Input | System Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Bell** | Show what is new since last look | Click the bell | A short list, with an unread watermark that moves to now. It also carries the admin-team alerts listed in 5.3 (sign-ups, enquiries, leads, subscriptions, deletion requests, listing activity and new listings) |
| **Recent Activity page** | Full timeline | "View all" | Dated timeline of recent marketing enquiries and listing leads, filterable by kind. Each row opens the right record. There is no per-item read state. |

4.20 Shared Aids Across Screens

| Aid | Where It Appears | What It Does |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Location search** | Post and edit forms, bulk upload | Google-based place search, map-link resolution and a check that the pin is inside the city |
| **Image and file upload** | Forms | Direct upload to storage with size and type limits |
| **PDF download** | Listing and project pages, invoices | Property, demand and project PDFs |
| **Email check** | Every form that takes an email | Format, disposable-domain and mail-server checks. A refused address names the field. |
| **Counts on every list** | Registers | Leads, relevancy and activity counts, computed the same way as in the customer app |
| **Server-side filters and sort** | Every register | Filters are applied on the server, so counts stay correct across pages |

##### 5\. Notifications and Emails the Panel Sends

###### 5.1 Emails to Operators (internal mail)

Subjects carry an environment label (for example "\[PROD\]") and replies go to the monitored contact inbox. These are never held back by the non-production recipient allow-list.

| Email | Trigger | Recipient |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **One-time password** | Operator created, or credentials reset | The operator |
| **Sign-in code** | Two-factor sign-in | The operator |
| **Password reset code** | Forgot password (off in production) | The operator |
| **Security alerts** | New device, super admin sign-in, repeated failures, password change, credential reset, role or permission change | The operator, plus the DevOps group on UAT and production |
| **Role change notice** | Role assignment changed | The operator |
| **Daily admin newsletter** | Every day at 08:00 India time | Every active super admin and admin |
| **Daily error digest** | Every day at 08:30 India time | Configured recipients (the "Daily New" newsletter and the digest are separate emails) |

> **Where technical and ops mail goes *(added, interim until the Google groups accept outside senders)*:** technical mail (alarms, error digest, security alert copy, deploy mail) goes to `tech@keydemand.in` on UAT and PROD since 2026-11-01. PROD also keeps the DevOps group as a second alarm and budget recipient. DEV and SIT send none. Business ops mail goes to `ops@keydemand.in` on PROD, `himanshu@keydemand.in` on UAT and `john.a@futuristglobal.com` on DEV and SIT (since 2026-10-31). Wherever this document says "DevOps group", read `tech@keydemand.in` for UAT and PROD.

###### 5.2 Notifications to Customers and Staff Triggered by Panel Actions

| Action | Who Is Notified | Through |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Listing posted on someone's behalf | The poster (property or demand posted notice) | Customer notification channels |
| Demand posted on a brand's behalf | The brand's active users | Customer notification channels |
| POC assigned to an account | The Keydemand member | In-app and other channels |
| Marketing lead assigned | The Keydemand member | In-app |
| High-value lead assigned, reassigned or withdrawn | The assigned Keydemand members | In-app. Several changes at once collapse into one summary. |
| High-value lead released | Subscribed, covered agents with a matching live property | In-app, linking to that property. Never worded "high-value". Never sent twice for the same lead. |
| Complimentary subscription granted | The agent | Same "subscription activated" notice as a purchase |
| Listing approved or rejected | The owner (per the lifecycle design; delivery not separately verified) | Customer notification channels |
| Agent requests contact on a Keydemand-held brand demand *(added)* | The brand's users and its Keydemand team | In-app and other customer channels |
| Contact request left unanswered *(added)* | Reminder at 48 h to the responders; "expired" notice to the requester at 72 h | Customer notification channels |

> **Messaging hold:** On DEV and SIT, email is held. Panel actions still succeed and the mail is only logged, so no sign-in code arrives there unless the address is on the allow-list.
