##### 6\. Feature Switches and Environment Differences

| Setting | DEV | SIT | UAT | PROD | Effect on the Panel |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Two-factor sign-in** | Off unless switched on by ops | Same | Same | **On** | A code is emailed after the password. Ops can change it without a deploy. No screen changes it. |
| **Forgot-password self-service** | On | On | On | **Off** | In production a super admin resets credentials |
| **Listing auto-approval** | On | On | On | **Off** | Customer posts wait for moderation in production. Panel posts on behalf are always auto-approved. |
| **Old "legacy proxy" admin routes** | Available | Available | Available | **Off** | Production exposes only the Control Panel API |
| **Enforce agent subscription on panel posts** | Off by default | Off by default | Off by default | Set per environment | When on, a post or bulk row for an agent needs coverage or the one free listing |
| **Messaging hold** | Email, WhatsApp, SMS held | Same | Push only | Off | Held mail is logged, not sent |
| **Security alert copy to DevOps group** | Off | Off | On | On | Extra copy of every security alert |
| **Relevancy v4 "Weighted" scoring** | On | On | On | On | Used on every match panel in the panel |
| **API documentation page** | On | On | On | Off | Interactive docs only outside production |
| **Presence tracking** | On | On | On | On | Powers the Live view. Can be switched off. |
| **Session idle limit** | 24 hours | 24 hours | 24 hours | 24 hours | Same everywhere |
| **Web signals intake** *(added)* | Per-environment setting | Same | Same | Off unless set | When off, the Acquisition view's visitor and funnel numbers stay empty. Changed by ops in AWS Parameter Store, live within about 30 seconds. No Control Panel screen. |
| **Sign-up attribution** *(added)* | Per-environment setting | Same | Same | Off unless set | When off, new accounts carry no campaign or platform, so the Campaigns part stays empty. Same runtime switch mechanism. |

> **Two-factor on a fresh environment:** the other panel automation (regression harnesses) cannot sign in with two-factor on until they handle the code step.

> **Messaging hold update *(added)*:** on DEV and SIT, email to the business-ops address is now let through the hold (the only address that is). Push stays on in DEV, SIT and UAT through the non-production Firebase project.

###### 9.3 Product Questions

1. **Should the Contributor be able to approve its own uploads?** Today it cannot, which enforces two-person control.  
2. **Should an Admin be able to see Technical Insights by default?** Today yes. The Tech Viewer role exists for engineers.  
3. **Should the assign-lead action on High Value Leads use the "unlock" permission?** Today it needs "manage rules", which means someone allowed to release leads may not be allowed to assign them.  
4. **Should email-domain rules and staff management share one permission?** Today both need "Control Panel Users — manage".  
5. **Should deleted HVL rules be restorable?** Today they are not.  
6. **Should demands posted by the panel also respect the agent subscription by default?** Today it is off unless an environment sets it.  
7. **Who receives the admin-team emails in 5.3?** Options are a shared inbox, every active super admin and admin (as with the daily newsletter), or a configurable list. It is also open whether bell alerts should follow role permissions, for example showing sign-up alerts only to operators with Users — view.  
8. **How should high-volume activity alerts be handled?** Contact viewed, images requested, contact requested and phone number viewed fire on every action and could flood the bell. Options are per-event, batched, or a separate filter on Recent Activity.  
9. **When do the daily summary emails go out?** New demands, new properties and new projects send one email a day. Confir

### Business rules extracted
- **BR-PD-1574** — The Control Panel is Keydemand's internal operations console; end customers never see it. _(1. Purpose and Who Uses It)_
- **BR-PD-1575** — Customers who cannot self-register (developers, operators, enterprise brands and tenants) are onboarded by staff in User Management / Enterprise. _(1. What It Is For)_
- **BR-PD-1576** — Control Panel operators sign in with email and password and share no sign-in with the customer app. _(1. Two separate identities)_
- **BR-PD-1577** — Keydemand team members who use the customer app are managed from the panel but sign in to the app with phone and code. _(1. Two separate identities)_
- **BR-PD-1578** — There is no self-registration for operators; a super admin or admin creates the account. _(2.1 Credentials)_
- **BR-PD-1579** — New and reset operator accounts receive a one-time password by email. _(2.1 First sign-in)_
- **BR-PD-1580** — The first sign-in forces a password change and it cannot be skipped. _(2.1 First sign-in; 4.1 Forced password change)_
- **BR-PD-1581** — Password rule: at least 6 characters with one uppercase letter, one number and one special character; the form lists what is missing. _(2.1 Password rules)_
- **BR-PD-1582** — When two-factor is on for the environment, a 6-digit code is emailed after the password; it lasts 5 minutes and works once. _(2.1 Two-factor code)_
- **BR-PD-1583** — Two-factor is on in production. _(2.1; 6. Feature Switches)_
- **BR-PD-1584** — 5 wrong codes void the code. _(2.1 Code limits)_
- **BR-PD-1585** — Code resend is allowed after 60 seconds, up to 3 times. _(2.1 Code limits; 4.1 Resend code)_
- **BR-PD-1586** — At most 5 codes are issued per person in 15 minutes. _(2.1 Code limits)_
- **BR-PD-1587** — If code delivery fails, sign-in fails with a "try again" message; the system never lets someone in because email failed. _(2.1 Code delivery failure)_
- **BR-PD-1588** — 5 wrong passwords in a row lock the account for 15 minutes; it unlocks by itself and a correct sign-in resets the count. _(2.1 Password lockout)_

### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Analytics (Google Analytics tile) is a placeholder; permission exists, no screen.
- Content Management and Site Down permissions reserved for a later phase; no screen.
- No per-item read state on the bell; it uses a "last seen" time.
- Agent deletion is final; there is no admin undelete for agents. Deleted HVL rules cannot be restored.
- Two-factor cannot be switched from the panel; controlled from the AWS console by ops.
- Inferred, not verified: exact tabs/buttons on detail pages; role editor layout; Formats screen entry points; moderation notification delivery; which environments set enforce-agent-subscription on; exact production newsletter/digest recipients; Insights part lists (code manifest is source of truth); whether web signals and sign-up attribution are on in production (default off); final contact-request notification copy; undated changes after 2026-11-03 may be missing.

### Content
#### Admin Control Panel — End-to-End Functional Flows

> **Audience:** operations, customer success, QA and product. **Status date:** 2026-11-05. **Companion documents:** [01 — Product Documentation](./01-product-documentation.md) (access model, permissions, navigation, features) · [Operator persona flow](../personas/09-control-panel-operator.md) **Reading guide:** each flow names the **actor**, what must be true first, the **steps** (with validations and success and failure outcomes), the **side effects** (notifications and audit), and **edge cases**. Permission names refer to the matrix in the product documentation.

##### Part A — Access and Staff

###### Flow 1 — Sign In With Password Only

- **Actor:** Any operator, in an environment where two-factor is off.  
- **Prerequisites:** An active operator account with a password already set.  
1. The operator opens the sign-in page and enters email and password.  
2. The system checks the credentials.  
3. **Success:** the console opens. Access and renewal tokens are stored. The operator lands on the Dashboard, or on the first screen their role allows.  
4. **Wrong credentials:** a clear error. After 5 wrong passwords in a row the account locks for 15 minutes, then unlocks by itself.  
5. **Disabled account:** sign-in is refused with a "disabled" message.  
- **Side effects:** a successful sign-in is logged. A sign-in from a new device or location, or by a super admin, emails a security alert (at most once an hour for the same case). The very first sign-in ever does not alert.  
- **Edge cases:** a correct sign-in resets the failure count. A person with no screens in their role is sent to the closest permitted screen, or sees nothing in the sidebar.

###### Flow 2 — Sign In With an Emailed Code (Two-Factor)

- **Actor:** Any operator in production, or in any environment where ops switched two-factor on.  
- **Prerequisites:** Flow 1 steps 1 to 2 succeed.  
1. After a correct password, the system emails a 6-digit code and shows the code screen with the masked email address.  
2. The operator enters the code within 5 minutes.  
3. **Success:** same as Flow 1 step 3\.  
4. **Wrong code:** an error shows how many attempts remain. After 5 wrong codes the code is void and the operator must sign in again. Wrong codes never lock the password.  
5. **Resend:** available after 60 seconds, at most 3 times. The old code stops working.  
6. **Expired, used or replaced code:** the operator is asked to sign in again.  
7. **Too many codes:** more than 5 codes in 15 minutes refuses further sign-ins for a while.  
8. **Email cannot be sent:** the sign-in fails with a "try again" message. The system never signs the operator in without the code.  
- **Side effects:** codes issued and failures are logged. Five wrong codes emails a security alert.  
- **Edge cases:** the switch is operational, so the screen follows what the server says each time, not a setting. A code issued while the switch was on is still honoured if it is switched off. A newer sign-in replaces any older open code. On environments that hold email, the sign-in succeeds into the code step but no email arrives.

###### Flow 3 — First Sign-In and Forced Password Change

- **Actor:** A newly created operator, or one whose credentials were reset.  
- **Prerequisites:** A one-time password emailed by Flow 6 or Flow 7\.  
1. The operator signs in with the one-time password. The code step is skipped this once, because the password itself was emailed.  
2. The system opens the "set password" screen. There is no skip.  
3. The operator enters a new password twice. It must have at least 6 characters, one uppercase letter, one number and one special character. The form shows what is missing.  
4. **Success:** the password changes, every session (including this one) is replaced, and the console opens. The one-time password stops working.  
5. **Weak password:** refused with the missing requirements listed.  
- **Side effects:** a password-change security alert is emailed.  
- **Edge cases:** from the next sign-in, the code step applies where two-factor is on.

###### Flow 4 — Forgot Password

- **Actor:** An operator who cannot sign in.  
- **Prerequisites:** Self-service reset is switched on. **It is off in production.**  
1. The operator opens "Forgot password" and enters their email.  
2. The system always answers "if the account exists, a code was sent", to avoid revealing which emails exist.  
3. If the account is active, a 6-digit code is emailed. It lasts 15 minutes.  
4. The operator enters the email, the code and a new password.  
5. **Success:** the password changes, all sessions end, open sign-in codes are voided, and the operator signs in again.  
6. **Wrong code or weak password:** refused with a message.  
7. **Production:** the operator is told to ask a super admin, who uses Flow 7 (reset credentials).  
- **Side effects:** password reset alert emailed.

###### Flow 5 — Session Renewal, Idle Sign-Out and Sign Out Everywhere

- **Actor:** Any signed-in operator.  
- **Prerequisites:** A signed-in session.  
1. While the operator works, the session renews itself quietly before the 30-minute access expires. The operator notices nothing.  
2. If the operator is idle for 24 hours, the next click returns them to sign-in.  
3. **Sign out:** ends this device only.  
4. **Sign out everywhere:** ends every device and invalidates all tokens at once.  
5. **Disabled, role changed or password changed elsewhere:** the next click on any device sends the operator to sign-in.  
6. **Old session token reused:** treated as theft. The session ends everywhere and the event is logged.  
- **Edge cases:** several tabs refreshing at the same moment are tolerated for a few seconds. Tokens issued before the current session model are rejected, so everyone signs in once after that release.

###### Flow 6 — Create a Control Panel Operator

- **Actor:** Admin or super admin, with "Control Panel Users — manage".  
- **Prerequisites:** The new person's name, email and intended role.  
1. Open **Control Panel Users** and choose to add a user.  
2. Enter name, email, optional phone and city, and choose a role.  
3. The email is checked: format, disposable domain and mail-server lookup. A refused address names the field.  
4. Rules apply: an admin cannot create a super admin, and cannot give a role a permission they lack themselves. A third active super admin is refused.  
5. **Success:** the account is created with "must change password" set, a one-time password is emailed, and the list shows "pending sign-in".  
- **Side effects:** a role-assignment email goes to the new operator. The action is logged.  
- **Edge cases:** a duplicate email is refused. A held email on non-production environments is logged, and the action still succeeds.

###### Flow 7 — Disable, Enable, Reset or Delete an Operator

- **Actor:** Admin or super admin (delete is super admin only).  
- **Prerequisites:** The operator exists.  
1. **Disable:** open the operator and deactivate. The person's sessions end immediately and their open sign-in codes are voided. You cannot disable yourself or the last active super admin.  
2. **Enable:** reactivate. Old sessions do not return, so the person signs in again.  
3. **Reset credentials:** a new one-time password is emailed, "must change password" is set again, sessions end and a security alert is sent. A super admin may reset their own account. An admin cannot reset another super admin.  
4. **Delete:** super admin only. The account is soft-deleted and sessions end. Refused for yourself, for the last super admin, and for an operator who holds a parked Keydemand hand-over.  
5. **Change role:** edit the operator. A role change emails the operator and is logged.  
- **Edge cases:** only a super admin may move someone into or out of the super admin role. Super admins are limited to two active.

###### Flow 8 — Create or Edit a Custom Role

- **Actor:** Admin or super admin.  
- **Prerequisites:** A clear list of the screens and actions the role needs.  
1. Open **Control Panel Users**, then the Roles area, and choose to add a role.  
2. Name the role and tick permissions. Permissions are grouped by module, for example Users, Listings, Bulk Upload and App Insights.  
3. An admin only sees, and can only grant, permissions they hold themselves.  
4. **Success:** the role can be assigned in Flow 6 or Flow 7\. A permission edit takes effect on the holders' next click. The security address is emailed about the change.  
5. **Duplicate name or unknown permission:** refused.  
6. **Built-in roles:** super admin's set is fixed. Editing Admin, Contributor, Business Viewer or Tech Viewer is super admin only, and their names are fixed.  
- **Edge cases:** viewer roles for Insights give no Observability access. A role with Insights export but no view permission for the section cannot export that section.

---

##### Part B — User Management

###### Flow 9 — Agents: Create, Edit, Suspend, Reactivate, Delete

- **Actor:** Operator with the relevant Users permission.  
- **Prerequisites:** For create, the agent's name and phone.  
1. **Create:** open **Property Agents**, add an agent. Enter name and phone (required; Indian mobile only: +91 and 10 digits starting 6 to 9, from 2026-10-30; anything else is refused with the field named, before the duplicate-phone check) and optional email, company, designation, experience, cities, states, asset classes, transaction types, WhatsApp opt-in and picture. The account is pre-approved. A phone already in use is refused. A bad email is refused.  
2. **Edit:** change any detail, including phone (checked for uniqueness) and picture.  
3. **Suspend:** choose a reason. The agent's active properties, demands and projects go down. Open requests close and high-value leads for their demands are withdrawn. The result reports what was deactivated.  
4. **Reactivate:** restores exactly what the suspension took down. It does not undo a deletion.  
5. **Delete:** soft delete. Listings are deleted, the subscription ends, the phone is released for reuse and the agent can never sign in to the app again. There is no undo.  
6. **Review activity:** the agent page shows properties, demands, leads received, enquiries both ways and numbers viewed.  
- **Side effects:** all changes are logged. A pending deletion request is marked handled if the operator deletes the user directly.  
- **Edge cases:** reactivating a deleted agent does not restore login. Suspend is for pauses, delete is final.

###### Flow 10 — Individual Tenants and Occupiers

- **Actor:** Operator with Users permissions.  
- **Prerequisites:** The asset class is office or managed space. Retail and F\&B go through the brand flow.  
1. **Create:** pick the asset class, enter name, phone (Indian mobile only: +91 and 10 digits starting 6 to 9, from 2026-10-30; anything else is refused with the field named, before the duplicate-phone check) and company or brand name. Add optional email, city, transaction type and WhatsApp opt-in. A wrong asset class or a duplicate phone is refused.  
2. **Edit:** change details. For an office tenant, a setting decides whether they may post managed-space demands (default yes). The customer cannot change it themselves.  
3. **Suspend or delete:** same cascade as agents. Deleting an enterprise account holder deletes colleagues, their listings and the company. Deleting a member moves their listings to the holder.  
4. **Members (enterprise only):** add a colleague with name, phone (Indian mobile only: +91 and 10 digits starting 6 to 9, from 2026-10-30; anything else is refused with the field named, before the duplicate-phone check) and optional email. A duplicate phone is refused, and an individual tenant is refused. The account holder cannot be removed.  
5. **Convert and POC:** see Flow 14\.

###### Flow 11 — Brands: Create, Edit, Deactivate, Delete, Restore, Merge

- **Actor:** Operator with Users permissions.  
- **Prerequisites:** For create, brand name, asset class (retail or F\&B) and a primary user with name and phone.  
1. **Create:** add a brand as individual or enterprise. Enterprise also needs city and locality. One step creates the company, brand, primary user and any extra users. All phones are checked first. If any step fails, everything created is rolled back. Every phone, including the primary and any extra users, must be an Indian mobile (+91 and 10 digits starting 6 to 9) and is checked first, with the field named (primaryUser.mobile or the extra user's mobile).  
2. **Edit:** change name, display name, about, asset class, cities, transaction types, logo and cover. Individual brands also edit contact person, phone and email. Enterprise brands edit head-office city, locality, preferred locations, account-handler details and the AI-layer switch. A field that does not apply to that kind is refused with its name. The kind itself cannot be edited here.  
3. **Possible duplicates:** open the duplicates page. Each pair can be marked "not a duplicate", or merged by moving users into the other brand. When a merge empties a brand, its Keydemand-posted demands move too.  
4. **Deactivate:** members and their properties go down. **Reactivate:** revives only members this deactivation switched off.  
5. **Delete:** soft-deletes the brand, its users, their properties and demands, and the company when it was the last brand. Every count is shown. **Restore:** reverses exactly that delete. Restored listings return as inactive.  
6. **Remove a member:** their listings pass to the account holder. Refused for the account holder or the only member. **Add a user to an enterprise brand:** the mobile must be an Indian mobile, as in step 1.  
- **Side effects: all steps logged. A new Retail/F\&B brand sign-up notifies the admin team (Flow 38).**  
- **Edge cases:** renaming an individual brand also renames the customer's company and display name while they still match the old name.

###### Flow 12 — Developers and Managed Space Operators

- **Actor:** Operator with Users permissions.  
- **Prerequisites:** A sales conversation or an inbound lead (Flow 23).  
1. **Create:** open **Developers** or **Managed Space Operators** and add. Name, phone, company, designation, city and official email are required. GST or CIN is optional.  
2. The account is created already approved, with its company.  
3. If the same phone has a pending sign-up of the same role, that sign-up is approved and updated instead of refused. Any other holder of the phone is refused, and the message names the holder's role.  
4. **Edit:** change personal details, or the company name and logo.  
5. **Suspend or delete:** projects and centres go down, or are deleted. Other owners' properties tagged to a deleted project are unlinked.  
6. **Post supply for them:** use "Add project" on a developer or "Add centre" on an operator (Flow 18).  
- **Edge cases:** the register hides old pending sign-ups unless a filter asks for them.

###### Flow 13 — Keydemand Members: Create, Permissions, Hand-Over, Deactivate, Delete

- **Actor:** Operator with Users permissions.  
- **Prerequisites:** For create, name, a valid Indian mobile number (+91 and 10 digits starting 6 to 9), and a sub-role.  
1. **Create:** add a member with name, phone (Indian mobile, as above) and sub-role (Keydemand Agent or BRM). Optional email, designation, cities and permissions. With no permissions chosen, the member follows the role template.  
2. **Edit:** change details, phone or picture.  
3. **Set permissions:** toggle the 14 customer-app permissions. This creates a personal override. **Reset to template** removes it. Dashboard and Explore Property cannot be removed.  
4. **Edit a template:** open Roles and change a sub-role's defaults. This changes every member who follows it.  
5. **Deactivate or delete:** the panel first shows the member's **book**: accounts (POC or team), listings they posted, records assigned to them, high-value rules and leads, open leads and pending enquiries.  
6. If the book is not empty, the operator completes the **Hand over their work first** step by choosing one of two options.  
   1. **A Keydemand member:** everything moves now. The successor must be an active member and not the leaver.  
   2. **Hold with an admin:** nothing moves yet. A custodian (a Control Panel admin, preselected as the signed-in one) holds the work. This allows deactivation but not deletion.  
7. **Complete a held hand-over later:** open **Pending hand-overs**, choose the held item and pick an active member. The work moves and the item is marked complete.  
8. **Delete:** needs a real hand-over, not just a hold. Accounts must be reassigned first. Listings the member posted stay live as Keydemand listings.  
- **Side effects:** counts moved or custodian recorded in the audit trail.  
- **Edge cases:** work that arrives during the flow is counted again at the final step, so the action can be refused again. A hand-over from an already-inactive member is allowed, as a clean-up. Activating a member does not bring the work back. An operator holding a hand-over cannot be deleted (Flow 7).

###### Flow 14 — Enterprise Conversion, POC and Keydemand Team

- **Actor:** Operator with "Users — edit".  
- **Prerequisites:** An individual brand or tenant to promote, or an enterprise one to change. A POC must be an **active** Keydemand member.  
1. **Promote:** open the account and choose convert to enterprise. Optionally pick the POC in the same step.  
2. The POC is checked **before anything is written**. A bad or non-Keydemand POC stops the whole conversion.  
3. **Success:** demands and contact views become unlimited, multi-user access opens, and for a tenant a company is created if missing. If a POC was chosen it applies to every member, the account's team is set, and the POC is notified.  
4. **Demote:** choose convert to individual. The screen lists what is revoked: unlimited demands, unlimited contact views, self-management block lifted, formats for the customer's own users. Free contact views reset. If extra members exist, the action is refused unless forced, in which case colleagues are deactivated (not deleted). Brands also need a contact person and phone, taken from the primary user.  
5. **Nothing is taken down on demotion.** All members' listings move to the account holder, and the POC is kept.  
6. **Assign, change or clear the POC (brand):** open the POC dialog. The panel first shows the impact: demands, pending enquiries, contact unlocks and high-value leads. Optionally move the brand's demands to the new POC. If someone else changed the POC meanwhile, the dialog is refused as stale.  
7. **Assign POC (tenant):** only enterprise tenants can be assigned. Clearing works for any kind.  
8. **Keydemand team:** pick active members to work beside the POC.  
9. **Reassign a leaver's accounts:** from the Keydemand member, move all their accounts to another member or to nobody.  
- **Side effects:** the POC is notified. The audit trail records POC changes. The customer's own Relationship Manager card now shows the POC. A departed or deactivated POC shows as unassigned to the customer. Adding an enterprise user from the panel, or converting an individual to enterprise, notifies the admin team (Flow 38).  
- **Edge cases:** deactivating a member does not clear their accounts, because a suspension may be temporary. The panel shows a warning with the count instead.

###### Flow 15 — Enterprise Brand Onboarding With POC, Brand Users and Brand Demands

- **Actor:** Operator with Users and Listings permissions.  
- **Prerequisites:** Signed enterprise deal (offline), brand details and the people who will use the app.  
1. **Create the brand** as enterprise (Flow 11 step 1), including head-office city and locality, and the primary and any extra users. Everything is pre-approved.  
2. **Assign the POC** and, if needed, the Keydemand team (Flow 14).  
3. **Create formats:** open the brand's formats and add each reusable template (name, asset class, end use, size, store type, floor, possession, ceiling, frontage, documents, up to 10 cities).  
4. **Post demands for the brand:**  
   1. If the brand has users, post as one of them (Flow 17).  
   2. If the brand has no users yet, post as a Keydemand member **for the brand** (Flow 17 step 5).  
5. **Bulk demands:** upload a demand sheet for the brand with a Format column (Flow 21).  
6. **Review the brand's footprint:** the brand page shows demands filed under it or posted by members, relevancy, leads and a list of cities and localities with live demand counts.  
7. **Brand users** can themselves send help requests to their RM. With no RM assigned, the request goes to the operations inbox.  
8. **Contact requests on the brand's demands:** a demand Keydemand holds for the brand (migrated v1, posted on its behalf, or a Format post) no longer reveals a Keydemand member's phone to an agent. The agent's tap sends a contact request that the poster, the brand's users or the brand's Keydemand team can answer (Flow 24, step 6).  
- **Edge cases:** enterprise users receive no WhatsApp or email from the platform, only in-app and push. High-value routing applies to enterprise brands too.

---

##### Part C — Listings

###### Flow 16 — Post a Property on Behalf

- **Actor:** Operator with "Listings — edit".  
- **Prerequisites:** An active agent or Keydemand member as the poster. For an agent, a covering subscription if the "enforce subscription" switch is on.  
1. Open **Properties** and choose to post. Select who it is for. An "as agent" or "as Keydemand" option is available.  
2. The shared post form opens. Fill the asset class (retail, F\&B or office), transaction type, city, locality with a verified map pin, area, pricing and amenities.  
3. Add images: at least one each of interior, exterior and front side. Optional videos (up to 3 uploads and 3 links).  
4. **Validations:** the poster must be live. Only agents and Keydemand members can post properties. Managed space is refused (use a centre). The pin must be inside the chosen city. Lock-in cannot exceed lease tenure.  
5. If the agent is covered by the switch: needs coverage for the city and class, or the single free listing.  
6. **Success:** the property goes live immediately, already approved, with a published date. Server-owned fields (status, moderation, counters, boosters) cannot be set from the form.  
7. For a Keydemand poster, choose "Who can see this". At least one known group is required.  
- **Side effects: the poster is notified. The action is logged. The new property is shown to the admin team (Flow 38).**  
- **Edge cases:** if the operator saves it with images missing in a bulk context, see Flow 21\.

###### Flow 17 — Post a Demand on Behalf (Including for a Brand)

- **Actor:** Operator with "Listings — edit".  
- **Prerequisites:** A live poster whose persona may post that asset class.  
1. Open **Demands** and choose to post. Choose who it is for.  
2. The shared demand form opens. Fill asset class, transaction, city, locality, area or seats, possession, budget and class-specific needs.  
3. **Persona rules:** an occupier posts managed space only. An office tenant posts office or managed space. A brand posts only its own class. Developers and operators cannot post demands. Managed-space demands need at least 20 seats.  
4. **Success:** the demand goes live at once, already approved. It never expires under the current matching rules. High-value routing then runs (Flow 22).  
5. **Post for a brand with no users:** choose a Keydemand member as the poster and select the brand. The brand must be active, enterprise, not deleted, and of the demand's asset class. The demand is filed under the brand, flagged Keydemand-managed, and may name an active Keydemand member as assignee.  
   After posting, an agent who taps "View number" on this demand sends a contact request instead of seeing a number (Flow 24, step 6).  
6. **Audience:** only a Keydemand-posted demand chooses who sees it (developer, Keydemand team, agent). Other posters' demands default to agents plus Keydemand. A demand for an agent defaults to agents plus Keydemand.  
- **Side effects:** the poster, or for a brand demand the brand's active users, receive the "demand posted" notice. The action is logged. The new demand (including a managed space demand) is shown to the admin team (Flow 38).  
- **Edge cases:** the bulk route follows the same rules (Flow 21).

###### Flow 18 — Post a Developer Project or a Managed Centre

- **Actor:** Operator with "Projects — add".  
- **Prerequisites:** An active developer (for a project) or managed space operator (for a centre).  
1. Open the developer's or operator's page and choose **Add project** or **Add centre**.  
2. **Developer project required fields:** name, city, locality, state, developer name, transaction type, project type, status, asset classes (several allowed), project size, possession date unless ready to move, unit size range, efficiency, description, OC status, amenities, an image or a video, and a map link or pin. RERA ID is optional.  
3. **Managed centre:** lease only. Managed office needs seats and price per seat. Flex needs one or more formats, each with type, seats and price. Optional property-available-from, meeting rooms (yes or no), business hours, parking and so on.  
4. **Validation:** every problem is returned together. The poster must be a live developer (or operator for centres).  
5. **Success:** the project is created, with optional properties tagged to it.  
6. Later, use **Edit**, **Boosters**, tag or untag, **Delete** and **Restore** (Flow 20).  
- **Side effects:** logged. Tagged properties appear as the project's units. The new project is shown to the admin team (Flow 38).  
- **Edge cases:** project types "commercial" and "other" are no longer used. Old values are rewritten.

###### Flow 19 — Moderation: Approve or Reject

- **Actor:** Operator with "Listings — edit".  
- **Prerequisites:** Customer posts are waiting. In production moderation is on. On DEV, SIT and UAT posts are auto-approved, so the queue is mostly empty.  
1. Open **Properties** or **Demands** and switch to the moderation queue. Filter by pending, approved or rejected. Newest first.  
2. Open a listing to review all details, leads and matches.  
3. **Approve:** add an optional note. The listing becomes live with a published date. If it is a demand, high-value routing runs now and the result is shown.  
4. **Reject:** a reason is required. A live listing goes down. Open enquiries close. A demand's high-value lead is withdrawn.  
5. **Listings waiting in bulk review:** cannot be approved here. A message points to Bulk Upload review.  
6. **Already deleted listings:** cannot be moderated.  
- **Side effects:** logged. The owner is notified per the lifecycle design.  
- **Edge cases:** approving a previously rejected listing is the only way it returns. Owners cannot resubmit by editing.

###### Flow 20 — Edit, Disable, Delete a Listing; Project Delete, Restore, Untag, Boost

- **Actor:** Operator with the matching Listings or Projects permission.  
- **Prerequisites:** The listing exists.  
1. **Edit:** open **Edit** on a property, demand or project. The same shared form is used as in the customer app. The Control Panel can change fields that the customer's own edit locks after the first response. Fields owned by the system (IDs, v1 references, source) cannot be changed, and ignored fields are reported as warnings.  
2. **Enable or disable:** switch status. Enabling needs approval first. A listing waiting in bulk review cannot be switched.  
3. **Delete:** soft delete. A repeat delete reports not found.  
4. **Project delete:** unlinks tagged properties and reports how many. **Restore** re-links those not tagged elsewhere in the meantime. Older deletes carry no list, so none re-link.  
5. **Untag one unit:** removes the link between one property and the project.  
6. **Boost:** set featured, exclusive, sponsored, category (standard, premium, exclusive), an expiry for featured, and the assigned Keydemand POC.  
7. **Review leads and matches:** each listing has panels for leads and relevant matches.  
- **Side effects:** every change is logged. Demand status changes re-check high-value routing.  
- **Edge cases:** a demand that is reactivated gets a fresh "never expires" date under current rules.

###### Flow 21 — Bulk Upload End to End

- **Actor:** Uploader (permission "Bulk upload — upload") and Reviewer (permission "Bulk upload — review").  
- **Prerequisites:** Uploader also holds "Listings — edit" for demands and properties, or "Projects — add" for projects and centres. A sheet in the correct template.  
1. **Choose the variant** (demand by asset class, transaction and persona; Format-based demand for an enterprise brand; property; developer project; managed centre).  
2. **Download the template** or a sample, with Data, Instructions and Common-mistakes sheets and dropdown lists. Review the business rules in the information drawer.  
3. **Choose the poster:** one poster per file. For a brand with no users, choose a Keydemand member plus the brand. An optional per-row "poster phone" is a cross-check only: it must be the poster's own number, or a member of the same brand.  
4. **Upload** an .xlsx or .csv. Limits: 5 MB, 2,000 rows, 120 columns.  
5. **Duplicate file check:** the same file uploaded in the last 30 days asks for confirmation. A busy queue (2 active jobs per person, 5 overall) asks to try later.  
6. **Gate 1 — Validate:** the system checks every row against the strictest rules. Nothing is created. Each issue gives rule, column, cell reference, value, message and hint. Row results are valid, warning, error or duplicate. A file-level problem (wrong template, missing column) stops the job.  
7. **Review the report:** download the error report, fix the sheet and upload again, or **revalidate** (also after a 48-hour expiry).  
8. **Gate 2 — Create for review:** confirm the count of creatable rows. If the count changed since the preview, the system asks to reload. Each selected row is re-checked against fresh data. Rows that now fail are marked failed, and nothing is created for them. Warnings can be included or excluded. Duplicates are skipped unless included. Staged images are copied to the live image area.  
9. **Rows now exist but are hidden** from every list, search, count and customer view until approved.  
10. **Gate 3 — Approve or reject** (reviewer): open **Review**, filter by job, entity, pending or blocked, images pending, or high-value. Open a row to see the full listing, and fix it if needed through the normal edit form.  
11. **Approve:** selected rows, or all rows of a job. The stored listing is checked again. Demands get their expiry set and high-value routing runs. Projects get their staged tags applied. A property missing an interior, exterior or front image is **blocked** until images are added.  
12. **Reject:** a note is required. The row is soft-deleted and kept in the job history.  
13. **Cancel** a job before commit, if needed.  
- **Side effects:** counts, errors and approval results are kept on the job. Staging data is cleared 30 days after the job ends. The uploader and the reviewer are logged.  
- **Edge cases:** an agent with no plan takes their one free listing on the first valid row. Later rows are refused (when the enforce switch is on). An image link that fails is dropped with a warning. A reject of a bulk row gives back the free listing. The worker runs in the background and is retried up to 3 times.

---

##### Part D — Leads and Enquiries

###### Flow 22 — High Value Leads: Rules, City Switch and Lead Lifecycle

- **Actor:** Operator with the HVL permissions.  
- **Prerequisites:** The city is one of the eight Tier-1 cities (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi).  
1. **Define a rule:** choose city, asset class (retail, F\&B or office), a minimum size in square feet, an optional maximum, transaction type and the Keydemand members who will work its leads. A missing minimum, a non-Tier-1 city, or managed space is refused.  
2. **Save:** the system re-checks every live demand in that market. Demands that now qualify become leads. Demands that no longer qualify are withdrawn. Assignees are notified (one summary notice when many change).  
3. **How a demand becomes a lead:** it is posted by anyone except an agent, it is live and approved, it is not managed space, and it matches an active rule on city, class, transaction type and size (measured against carpet area). Enterprise brands are not exempt. An office demand above a city's own threshold also qualifies.  
4. **What happens to the demand:** it is hidden from agents. The poster's own audience choice is kept aside.  
5. **City switch:** turn a city on or off. All three asset classes in that city are re-checked together.  
6. **Lead register:** open **High Value Leads**. Filter by status, city, asset class, assignee, or search by lead ID or locality. Statuses are New, Assigned, Unlocked, Serviced, Expired and Withdrawn.  
7. **Assign:** choose who works the lead. A manual assignment wins over later rule changes. Withdrawn leads cannot be assigned.  
8. **Release (unlock):** open the demand to agents. Allowed at any time, even on a withdrawn lead, as long as the demand is still live and approved. Refused if the poster did not allow agents.  
9. **After release:** every agent can now see the demand, but only subscribed agents covering the city (including its region) and owning a live matching property are notified. The result reports how many were told and warns if none, or if the demand expires soon.  
10. **Take back (relock):** removes agent visibility only if the release added it. The lead returns to Assigned or New and is re-checked against current rules. If the demand is no longer live, the lead is withdrawn instead. Notices already sent and contacts already taken cannot be undone.  
11. **Delete a rule:** soft delete. Its leads are re-checked. Released leads are never retracted.  
- **Side effects:** assignees receive notices. Reconciliation results, including failures, are logged. A failure never undoes the rule change or the approval. Each new high-value lead notifies the admin team (Flow 38).  
- **Edge cases:** ending a demand in any way (delete, reject, deactivate, fulfil, expire) withdraws its lead. A rule with no assignees sends leads to the city's Keydemand members unless an admin deliberately emptied it.

###### Flow 23 — Marketing Enquiries and Onboarding Lead Conversion

- **Actor:** Operator with "Enquiries — view" and "Enquiries — manage".  
- **Prerequisites:** A lead arrived from the public site: developer or operator interest, enterprise solution, project interest, landing page or managed-office interest.  
1. Open **Marketing Enquiries**. Filter by type, status, city, assignee (including unassigned) or search. Repeated submissions from the same phone and role show as one lead with a submission count.  
2. Open a lead for details: name, phone, email, company, GST or CIN, city, asset class, message, project and assignee.  
3. **Assign:** choose an active Keydemand member. The member receives an in-app notice. A non-Keydemand or inactive person is refused. Unassign is allowed.  
4. **Change status:** New, Contacted or Closed.  
5. **Convert:** for developer or operator leads, create the account (Flow 12), then set the lead to **Converted** and link the customer's live account. The account must have the role the lead implies. Any other lead type cannot be converted.  
6. If the phone matches a pending sign-up of the same role, Flow 12 adopts it.  
- **Side effects: assignment notice. Logged. New enterprise, developer and operator enquiries notify the admin team (Flow 38).**  
- **Edge cases:** the shortcuts for developer, enterprise and operator leads open this page with the type filter set.

###### Flow 24 — Listing Leads Review

- **Actor:** Operator with "Enquiries — view".  
- **Prerequisites:** None.  
1. Open **Listing Leads** for every enquiry, contact request and image request on listings.  
2. Filter by status (pending, approved, rejected, expired, closed), type, city, who raised it, the listing's owner, dates and search. Tabs show totals regardless of the status filter.  
3. Each row names its listing with ID, title, city, locality, asset class, status and owner. A row whose listing is gone shows no listing.  
4. From a listing, a member or an agent, open the same list scoped to that item.  
5. For an agent, a separate "numbers viewed" list merges contact unlocks and enquiries per contacted listing.  
6. **Contact requests on a demand Keydemand holds for a brand (from 2026-11-03):**  
   1. When an agent taps "View number" on such a demand, no number is shown. A contact request is raised and appears here, on the demand's Leads tab and in the Received list of every responder.  
   2. **Who can answer:** the poster, the brand's users, or the brand's Keydemand team (POC and team members). Any Keydemand member can also answer. The first answer wins and a second is refused.  
   3. **What is shared:** the accepter's contact. If the brand hides its name, a brand user is shared as phone only, under "Retail brand" or "F&B brand".  
   4. The brand's own side tapping the button on its own demand gets no request and no charge. A Keydemand demand with no brand still reveals at once.  
   5. **No answer:** a reminder at 48 hours. At 72 hours the request expires and the viewer's free contact view is returned.  
   6. **Earlier views:** each phone view made on such a demand before this change was recorded as an accepted request (migration 129), so the lead history is complete. Nothing was sent and viewers keep the numbers they had.  
- **Side effects (contact requests):** the brand's users and Keydemand team are notified of a new request, the requester is notified when it expires.  
- **Edge cases:** the row's own city is often blank. Use the listing's city. Enquiries expire after 72 hours (a contact request is reminded at 48 hours, see step 6).  

###### Flow 25 — Account Deletion Requests

- **Actor:** Operator with "Users — view" (read), "Users — edit" (log, decline) and "Users — delete" (process).  
- **Prerequisites:** A request raised in the app, or one received by email.  
1. Open **Account Deletions**. Tabs show Requested, Processed, Declined and Withdrawn with counts. Filter by role, city or search.  
2. Open a request to see the person, their active listings, their active subscription and the full history.  
3. **Log an emailed request:** enter phone or user and an optional reason. A user already pending or deleted is refused.  
4. **Process:** the account is deleted like the normal delete. Listings go. The subscription ends (no automatic refund for a paid plan). The person is signed out. Refused if the request is no longer pending, or for enterprise members and Keydemand staff, who must be removed from their own screen.  
5. **Decline:** a note is required, and the user sees it.  
6. Deleting the last member of an individual brand through this route also deletes demands filed under that brand, closes their requests and withdraws their high-value leads.  
- **Side effects:** each transition is added to the request history. Logged. A new deletion request raised by a user notifies the admin team (Flow 38).  
- **Edge cases:** a request withdrawn by the user meanwhile makes the action fail with a clear message. A direct admin delete marks a pending request as handled.

##### Part E — Commercial and Configuration

###### Flow 26 — Subscription Setup: Cities, Regions, Pricing

- **Actor:** Operator with "Subscription — manage cities" and "Subscription — edit pricing".  
- **Prerequisites:** A pricing decision.  
1. **Add a city:** name, tier (metro, non-metro or rest of India), optional state, region, high-value size threshold. Duplicates are refused.  
2. **Edit a city:** change tier, threshold, active status or region. A city cannot be deleted, only deactivated. Moving an indicative city between tiers is blocked.  
3. **Regions:** assign or clear a region (Delhi NCR, Mumbai region, Goa, Pune region). Covering one city covers the region for posting and contact reveal, and browsing from any member shows the region.  
4. **Prices:** open **Price Management**. For each package (Retail & F\&B, Office), set the monthly rate for metro, non-metro, rest of India and Pan-India. Set the GST percentage (0 to 100).  
5. **Effect:** new prices apply to new purchases. A price edit is logged against the pricing record.  
- **Edge cases:** the "Rest of India" label and the legacy wildcard share one rate.

###### Flow 27 — Agent Subscription: Grant, Extend, Cancel, Revoke, Change Coverage

- **Actor:** Operator with "Users — view" and "Users — edit".  
- **Prerequisites:** An agent account.  
1. **Grant a free plan:** open the agent and choose grant. The default is Pan-India coverage for both packages for 30 days. Optionally scope coverage by city or region, and change the duration.  
2. **Same as a purchase:** the plan is active, the agent is told "subscription activated", and listings hidden after an earlier lapse reappear. The price is zero and no payment is taken.  
3. **Extend:** add days (up to 365). An expired plan is revived.  
4. **Cancel:** the plan ends at the end of its cycle. **Revoke now:** the plan expires immediately, the agent is downgraded and their listings are re-hidden.  
5. **Reactivate:** revives a cancelled or expired plan.  
6. **Change coverage:** replace the coverage list. On a paid plan, coverage can only be added to, never removed. Cities in one region are merged. Pan-India subsumes city entries for that package. A change made by someone else meanwhile asks the operator to reload.  
7. **Roster:** open the global subscription roster to filter by user, status or cycle end.  
8. **Enforce switch (when on):** a post or bulk row made for an agent needs coverage for the city and class (a covered city covers its region), or the agent's one free listing. A plan that is complimentary counts the same as a paid one. To post for an agent with no plan, grant a plan first.  
- **Edge cases:** managed space is never gated by subscription.

---

##### Part F — Configuration and Data

###### Flow 28 — Email-Domain Rules

- **Actor:** Operator with "Control Panel Users — manage".  
- **Prerequisites:** A domain to block or allow.  
1. Open **Email Domains**. Search a domain and filter by kind. A summary shows the built-in list size and the protected domains.  
2. **Check a domain** to see whether it is blocked, allowed or protected, and how many existing accounts use it.  
3. **Add:** paste up to 5,000 domains with a reason of up to 300 characters, as block or allow. Each domain is judged alone, and rejected lines come back with a reason (not a domain, protected, already present, or the opposite rule exists). Duplicates in the paste are dropped silently.  
4. **Remove:** rules cannot be edited. To change a rule's kind, remove it and add again.  
5. **Effect:** within about a minute on every service. Allow beats both lists and skips the mail-server lookup. A rule also covers sub-domains. Existing accounts keep working and only new or changed addresses are affected.  
- **Side effects:** each add or remove is logged.

###### Flow 29 — V1 Completion Queue and Migration

- **Actor:** Operator with "Listings — view" (properties queue) and "Users — view" (profiles queue).  
- **Prerequisites:** Data brought across from v1.  
1. Open **V1 Completion Queue**. Two tabs appear for the permissions the operator holds.  
2. **Properties tab:** migrated listings the edit form would refuse. Each row lists the missing fields, with counts by field. Filter by city, asset class or search.  
3. **Profiles tab:** migrated agents missing asset class, cities, email or a valid RERA number.  
4. Open a record, edit it in the normal edit screen and save. A complete record leaves the queue by itself.  
5. **Migration notes:** a migrated listing or project shows what happened to it. Native v2 records show nothing.  
6. **v1 numbers:** search by a v1 number, or by "V1" plus a number to match only v1. Old v1 links redirect to the v2 page. A v1 number cannot be edited.  
- **Engineering side (not in the panel):** one-off scripts move v1 data into a staging area, copy it between environments and apply a configuration baseline. Reviewers should ask engineering for these runs.  
- **Edge cases:** up to 5,000 records are read per queue call.

###### Flow 30 — Relevance Panels, Formats and Location Aids

- **Actor:** Operator with "Listings — view" and, for formats, "Formats — manage".  
- **Prerequisites:** A listing or brand.  
1. **Relevance:** on a property, see relevant demands and relevant projects. On a demand, see relevant properties and projects. On a project, see units and relevant demands. Each row shows a % Match from the same scoring as the customer app, and the same visibility rules (the panel sees every audience).  
2. **Formats:** on an enterprise brand, add, edit or deactivate formats. A format value that is invalid is refused with its field name. Formats are not limited by the brand's kind. A customer's own use of formats stops if the brand is demoted, and returns if it is promoted again.  
3. **Location aids:** while posting, search a place, resolve a pasted map link, reverse-geocode a pin, and check the pin is inside the chosen city.  
4. **File uploads:** pictures, logos, images, videos and documents go to storage with size and type checks.

###### Flow 31 — Dashboard

- **Actor:** Operator with "Dashboard — view".  
- **Prerequisites:** None.  
1. Open the Dashboard. Choose Today, Last 7 days or Last 30 days.  
2. **Primary outcomes** load first: high-value leads, enterprise enquiries by persona, project leads and Keydemand team, each with "new" and "total".  
3. **Secondary outcomes** load when expanded: subscriptions, users by role, demands, properties and projects by asset class and poster type, leads, marketing enquiries, deleted properties and account deletions.  
4. **Per-member view:** pick a Keydemand member to see their enterprise accounts, high-value leads, listings, projects and leads.  
5. **Detail block:** expand for register-level counts and asset-class donuts.  
6. Tiles link to the matching registers.  
- **Edge cases:** "Today" starts at midnight India time. Totals exclude deleted items except where the metric counts deletions. The same figures are in the morning email (Flow 34).

###### Flow 32 — App Insights, Export, Snapshots and Presence

- **Actor:** Operator with an Insights view permission. Export also needs the export permission.  
- **Prerequisites:** None.  
1. Open **App Insights** and choose Business or Technical (only the sections the operator may see appear).  
2. **Business:** pick a view, a date range (up to 366 days, with limits per view), granularity and comparison. Narrow by city, region, asset class and role. Internal and test accounts are excluded by default, and v1 data can be included. The Business views are Overview, Users and Growth, **Acquisition and Sign-ups**, Revenue and Subscriptions, Marketplace, Engagement and Leads, Cities and Regions, KD Team and Operations, and Live.  
   **Acquisition and Sign-ups (from 2026-11-05):** shows visitors landed, sign-ups opened, visit-to-sign-up rate and accounts registered (overall and from a campaign), the sign-up funnel overall and per persona, landing sources (campaign tags, referring sites, Facebook and Instagram in-app browsers), sign-up and sign-in refusals by step, error code and field, and new accounts by campaign, source and platform. The traffic parts cover 7 days at most, show cells under 5 as "<5", and fill only while web signals and sign-up attribution are switched on (ops runtime switches, live within about 30 seconds, off by default in production). Accounts created before attribution was on show as "not recorded". The visit-to-sign-up rate is approximate.  
3. **Technical:** pick a window (1 hour to 7 days, or custom up to 7 days) and optionally a service.  
4. The KPI strip loads first. Expand a card to load its trend, funnel, cohort or breakdown. Cards that run log searches are flagged, because they cost more.  
5. **Help:** the "?" icon explains each widget in business language.  
6. **Refresh:** the icon bypasses the 5-minute cache. The Live view refreshes only on request and caches for 30 seconds.  
7. **Live:** shows who is online now, signed in or not, active in 30 and 60 minutes, by platform, role and city, and which screens are in use.  
8. **Export:** CSV or Excel for the whole view with the same filters. The file name carries the section, view and dates. Each export is logged with the row count.  
9. **Errors:** a range that is too large shows its own message. A widget that cannot be built shows as unavailable and the rest still renders. A Technical page stops waiting at 45 seconds.  
10. **Snapshots:** every night at 00:15 India time the system records a platform row and one row per city. This is the only history behind active-user, live-supply, open-demand and paying-agent trends.  
11. **Presence:** every signed-in customer action stamps their last activity (at most every 15 minutes), which powers Live.  
- **Edge cases:** snapshot-based trends show no change when a role, asset class or internal-account filter is applied, and a caveat says so. Groups under 5 people show as "under 5". The Technical Runtime Config view is read-only.

###### Flow 33 — Observability Settings

- **Actor:** Super admin only ("Observability — manage").  
- **Prerequisites:** A troubleshooting need.  
1. Open **Observability**. Each service shows its current log level and any expiry.  
2. **Change a level:** choose service and level (fatal, error, warn, info, debug, trace) and give a reason. Applies within about 30 seconds.  
3. **Debug and trace** always need an expiry (maximum 240 minutes) and cannot be set on the default level. The expiry counts down on screen.  
4. **Debug for specific users:** target a limited number of customers for detailed logs.  
5. **Clear overrides** to return to normal.  
6. **Error digest:** switch the daily email on or off, edit recipients, choose whether to send when there were no errors, and give a reason.  
- **Side effects:** every change needs a reason and is logged.  
- **Edge cases:** the two-factor switch is not here. Ops change it in the cloud console.

###### Flow 34 — Daily Newsletter and Error Digest

- **Actor:** Automatic. Recipients are admins and configured addresses.  
- **Prerequisites:** The scheduled jobs are enabled (they are on in production).  
1. **08:00 India time:** the daily "new" dashboard summary is emailed to every active super admin and admin. Contributor and custom roles are excluded. It uses the same figures as the Dashboard.  
2. **08:30 India time:** the daily error digest is emailed to the configured recipients. It lists the previous India day's errors, failed jobs and alarm changes. When everything succeeded it says so (if "send when clean" is on).  
3. A record of each newsletter run is kept. A setting can switch newsletter delivery to "log only".  
4. **00:15 India time:** the daily insights snapshot (Flow 32).  
5. **Every 30 minutes:** the payment reconciliation job settles missed payments. Subscription expiry runs once a day at about 06:00 India time.  
- **Edge cases:** in production a missing daily digest raises an alarm that emails the technical address (`tech@keydemand.in` on UAT and production since 2026-11-01, with the DevOps group kept as a second alarm recipient on production).
- **Where the mail goes (interim, until the Google groups accept outside senders):** technical mail (alarms, digest, security alert copy) goes to `tech@keydemand.in` on UAT and production, and nothing on DEV and SIT. Business ops mail goes to `ops@keydemand.in` (production), `himanshu@keydemand.in` (UAT) and `john.a@futuristglobal.com` (DEV and SIT).  
- **Job diagnostics (from 2026-11-01):** a job that crashes now writes a failure record, and a job that carries on past failing items (digest, newsletter, incomplete-registration notices) is flagged partial, which raises the `scheduled-job-partial` alarm (production emails). What the jobs do is unchanged.  

###### Flow 35 — PDF Download

- **Actor:** Operator with "Listings — view" (or "Projects — view" for projects).  
- **Prerequisites:** The PDF service is configured in the environment.  
1. On a property, demand or project page, choose **Download PDF**.  
2. The system builds a branded PDF from the listing. The same document is cached, so repeats are fast.  
3. **Success:** the file downloads.  
4. **Service not configured:** the panel shows that documents are unavailable.  
- **Edge cases:** an audience-restricted property is allowed because the panel sees every audience.

###### Flow 36 — Bell and Recent Activity

- **Actor:** Any signed-in operator.  
- **Prerequisites:** None.  
1. Click the bell to see the latest items and an unread count.  
2. The "last seen" time moves to now when the operator looks.  
3. **View all:** opens the timeline of recent marketing enquiries, listing leads and admin team notifications (Flow 38), grouped by day, filterable by kind.  
4. Each row opens the matching enquiry, listing or lead.  
- **Edge cases:** there is no mark-as-read on single items. The panel has no notification store of its own. The new admin team notifications (Flow 38\) will need one for their bell items and unread count.

###### Flow 37 — Audit Trail and Security Alerts

- **Actor:** Automatic.  
- **Prerequisites:** None.  
1. Every action that changes data records who did it, what changed, the target, and the time. See the product documentation for the list of areas.  
2. Refused privileged actions (such as an admin trying to touch a super admin) are logged as refusals.  
3. Security events send alert emails (Flow 1 side effects).  
4. Some audit rows carry counts: cascades on delete, hand-over counts, reconciliation counts, export row counts.  
- **Edge cases:** no audit screen appears in the sidebar today (see open questions).

###### **Flow 38 — Admin Team Notifications (Email and Bell)**

* **Actor:** Automatic. Recipients are the admin team (see product questions). This flow is a new specification (2026-11-03) and was checked again on 2026-11-05: no admin-team notification store, event or send is in the code yet, so this flow is still a specification only.  
* **Prerequisites:** The trigger event happens on the platform (website, app or Control Panel).  
1. When a trigger event in the table below happens, the system adds an item to the admin bell (Flow 36).  
2. Where the event has an email, the system also emails the admin team. Most emails go out as soon as the event happens.  
3. New demands, new properties and new projects send one daily summary email with the count and the cities. The bell still shows each item as it is posted.  
4. Activity events (contact viewed, image requested, contact requested, phone number viewed) are bell-only. They send no email.  
5. Each email points the reader to the admin panel. Each bell item opens the matching user, listing, lead or request.  
* **Side effects:** none beyond the email and the bell item.  
* **Edge cases:** "Enterprise user added" (from the Control Panel) and "Enterprise user converted" (individual to enterprise) are separate events. "Agent subscribed" fires for new, renewal and auto-pay purchases and says which one it is. Some emails carry phone numbers (developer and operator enquiries, pending sign-ups, deletion requests, project leads).

###### Inferred Rather Than Verified

| Item | What Was Not Confirmed |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Exact button labels** | Taken from page headers and the admin guide, not from a running app. |
| **Step order in Flow 11 (duplicates merge)** | Described from the duplicates page and the guide. The merge dialog was not walked through. |
| **Moderation notifications to owners** | Present in the lifecycle design. Delivery was not verified in code. |

| **Newsletter and digest recipients in production** | Newsletter goes to active super admins and admins. Digest recipients come from settings. The live values were not checked. |
| **Job times in India time** | Newsletter 08:00, error digest 08:30, subscription expiry about 06:00 and the snapshot at 00:15. Derived from the production schedule rules (which are in UTC), not observed running. |
| **Bulk upload worker retries** | The guide and engineering notes say up to 3 attempts. Not observed running. |
| **Acquisition view on production** | The view and its help exist in code. Whether web signals and sign-up attribution are switched on in production was not checked. |

| **Changes after 2026-11-03** | Only changes with a dated note in the repo were captured. |

###### Product Questions

1. **Should there be an in-panel audit viewer?** Staff currently cannot see who changed what.  
2. **Should assigning a high-value lead need the same permission as releasing it?**  
3. **Should a Contributor be able to see why its bulk rows were rejected?** Today they appear in the job history.  
4. **Should operators get a "who is signed in" view?** Sessions exist but have no screen.  
5. **Should enterprise users receive any WhatsApp or email?** Today none, by decision.  
6. **Who exactly receives the admin team notifications (Flow 38)?** Every active super admin and admin, a shared address, or a list per event? Can a role or person opt out of an event?  
7. **When do the daily new demands, properties and projects emails go out?** Should they join the 08:00 newsletter (Flow 34\) or be separate emails? Should “today” use the India day, as the Dashboard does?  
8. **Should notification emails carry phone numbers?** Developer and operator enquiries, pending sign-ups, deletion requests and project leads include one. A masked number with a link to the panel would keep personal data out of inboxes.  
9. **How should high-volume bell events be handled?** Contact viewed, image requested, contact requested and phone number viewed can fire many times a day. Should they be grouped, filtered by kind, or kept for a set period? What counts as a “pending sign-up”, and which flow approves it?

### Business rules extracted
- **BR-PD-1861** — After successful password sign-in, access and renewal tokens are stored and the operator lands on the Dashboard or the first screen their role allows. _(Flow 1 step 3)_
- **BR-PD-1862** — A disabled account is refused at sign-in with a "disabled" message. _(Flow 1 step 5)_
- **BR-PD-1863** — A security alert for a new device/location or a super admin sign-in is emailed at most once an hour for the same case; the very first sign-in ever does not alert. _(Flow 1 side effects)_
- **BR-PD-1864** — A successful sign-in is logged. _(Flow 1 side effects)_
- **BR-PD-1865** — An operator whose role has no screens is sent to the closest permitted screen or sees nothing in the sidebar. _(Flow 1 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-1866** — After a correct password with two-factor on, a 6-digit code is emailed and the code screen shows the masked email address. _(Flow 2 step 1)_
- **BR-PD-1867** — A wrong code shows the attempts remaining; after 5 wrong codes the code is void and the operator must sign in again; wrong codes never lock the password. _(Flow 2 step 4)_
- **BR-PD-1868** — Resending a code makes the old code stop working. _(Flow 2 step 5)_
- **BR-PD-1869** — An expired, used or replaced code asks the operator to sign in again. _(Flow 2 step 6)_
- **BR-PD-1870** — More than 5 codes in 15 minutes refuses further sign-ins for a while. _(Flow 2 step 7)_
- **BR-PD-1871** — Codes issued and failures are logged; five wrong codes emails a security alert. _(Flow 2 side effects)_
- **BR-PD-1872** — The two-factor screen follows what the server says each time; a code issued while the switch was on is still honoured if it is switched off. _(Flow 2 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-1873** — A newer sign-in replaces any older open code. _(Flow 2 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-1874** — On environments that hold email, sign-in reaches the code step but no email arrives. _(Flow 2 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-1875** — With a one-time password the code step is skipped that once because the password itself was emailed. _(Flow 3 step 1)_
- **BR-PD-1876** — The new password must be entered twice. _(Flow 3 step 3)_
- **BR-PD-1877** — Setting the new password replaces every session (including this one) and the one-time password stops working. _(Flow 3 step 4)_
- **BR-PD-1878** — A password-change security alert is emailed on forced change. _(Flow 3 side effects)_
- **BR-PD-1879** — From the next sign-in the code step applies where two-factor is on. _(Flow 3 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-1880** — Forgot password always answers "if the account exists, a code was sent" to avoid revealing which emails exist. _(Flow 4 step 2)_
- **BR-PD-1881** — A reset code is emailed only if the account is active. _(Flow 4 step 3)_
- **BR-PD-1882** — Successful password reset ends all sessions and voids open sign-in codes. _(Flow 4 step 5)_
- **BR-PD-1883** — In production the forgot-password operator is told to ask a super admin, who uses reset credentials; a password reset alert is emailed. _(Flow 4 steps 7; side effects)_
- **BR-PD-1884** — The session renews itself before the 30-minute access expires. _(Flow 5 step 1)_
- **BR-PD-1885** — After 24 hours idle the next click returns the operator to sign-in. _(Flow 5 step 2)_
- **BR-PD-1886** — "Sign out everywhere" ends every device and invalidates all tokens at once. _(Flow 5 step 4)_
- **BR-PD-1887** — If disabled, role changed or password changed elsewhere, the next click on any device sends the operator to sign-in. _(Flow 5 step 5)_
- **BR-PD-1888** — Several tabs refreshing at the same moment are tolerated for a few seconds. _(Flow 5 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-1889** — Tokens issued before the current session model are rejected, so everyone signs in once after that release. _(Flow 5 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-1890** — Creating an operator needs "Control Panel Users — manage" and takes name, email, optional phone and city, and a role. _(Flow 6 steps 1-2)_
- **BR-PD-1891** — A new operator is created with "must change password" set, a one-time password emailed, and the list shows "pending sign-in". _(Flow 6 step 5)_
- **BR-PD-1892** — A role-assignment email goes to the new operator and the action is logged. _(Flow 6 side effects)_
- **BR-PD-1893** — A duplicate operator email is refused; a held email on non-production is logged and the action still succeeds. _(Flow 6 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-1894** — Disabling an operator voids their open sign-in codes as well as ending sessions. _(Flow 7 step 1)_
- **BR-PD-1895** — Enabling an operator does not bring old sessions back; the person signs in again. _(Flow 7 step 2)_
- **BR-PD-1896** — Reset credentials sets "must change password" again; a super admin may reset their own account; an admin cannot reset another super admin. _(Flow 7 step 3)_
- **BR-PD-1897** — Delete operator is refused for yourself, for the last super admin, and for an operator who holds a parked Keydemand hand-over. _(Flow 7 step 4)_
- **BR-PD-1898** — Custom role creation takes a name and ticked permissions, grouped by module (e.g. Users, Listings, Bulk Upload, App Insights). _(Flow 8 steps 1-2)_
- **BR-PD-1899** — An admin only sees, and can only grant, permissions they hold themselves. _(Flow 8 step 3)_
- **BR-PD-1900** — A custom-role permission edit takes effect on the holders' next click and the security address is emailed about the change. _(Flow 8 step 4)_
- **BR-PD-1901** — A duplicate role name or unknown permission is refused. _(Flow 8 step 5)_
- **BR-PD-1902** — Built-in role names are fixed; editing Admin, Contributor, Business Viewer or Tech Viewer is super admin only. _(Flow 8 step 6)_

- **BR-PD-2093** — The bell shows the latest items and an unread count, and "last seen" moves to now when the operator looks. _(Flow 36 steps 1-2)_
- **BR-PD-2094** — "View all" opens a timeline of marketing enquiries, listing leads and admin team notifications grouped by day, filterable by kind. _(Flow 36 step 3)_
- **BR-PD-2095** — There is no mark-as-read on single items and the panel has no notification store of its own; Flow 38 notifications will need one for bell items and unread count. _(Flow 36 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-2096** — Every data-changing action records who did it, what changed, the target and the time. _(Flow 37 step 1)_
- **BR-PD-2097** — Refused privileged actions are logged as refusals. _(Flow 37 step 2)_
- **BR-PD-2098** — Some audit rows carry counts: cascades on delete, hand-over counts, reconciliation counts, export row counts. _(Flow 37 step 4)_
- **BR-PD-2099** — Admin-team notification: trigger event adds an item to the admin bell, and where the event has an email the admin team is emailed, most as soon as the event happens. _(Flow 38 steps 1-2)_
- **BR-PD-2100** — Each admin-team email points the reader to the admin panel and each bell item opens the matching user, listing, lead or request. _(Flow 38 step 5)_
- **BR-PD-2101** — "Agent subscribed" fires for new, renewal and auto-pay purchases and says which one. _(Flow 38 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-2102** — Some admin-team emails carry phone numbers: developer and operator enquiries, pending sign-ups, deletion requests, project leads. _(Flow 38 edge cases)_
- **BR-PD-2103** — Flow 38 maps events to source flows: retail/F&B brand sign-up (11, 17), office/managed sign-up (10), managed space demand (17, 19), enterprise enquiry (23, 14), enterprise user added (14, 15), converted (14), developer/operator enquiry (23, 12), high-value lead (22), agent subscribed (26, 27), deletion request (25), project lead (24, 18), activity events (24), new demands (17, 19), properties (16, 19), projects (18). _(Flow 38 table)_
- **BR-PD-2104** — New retail/F&B brand sign-up, enterprise user added/converted and the new property, demand and project items are cross-referenced as side effects of Flows 11, 14, 16, 17, 18. _(Flow 11, 14, 16, 17, 18 side effects)_
- **BR-PD-2105** — New high-value lead notifies the admin team on each creation. _(Flow 22 side effects)_
- **BR-PD-2106** — New enterprise, developer and operator enquiries notify the admin team. _(Flow 23 side effects)_
- **BR-PD-2107** — A user-raised account deletion request notifies the admin team. _(Flow 25 side effects)_

### Open questions / ambiguities in this doc
- Flow 38 (admin team notifications) is a specification only (2026-11-03, rechecked 2026-11-05): no admin-team notification store, event or send exists in the code yet.
- Not built: audit viewer (engineering reads it from the database); Analytics screen (placeholder, no Google Analytics); un-delete of an agent; un-delete of an HVL rule; content management and site-down (permissions reserved); two-factor switch in the panel (cloud console, ops); draft clean-up and scheduled content jobs are not part of the panel.
- Inferred, not verified: exact button labels; step order in Flow 11 (duplicates merge dialog not walked through); moderation notifications to owners; which environments enforce agent subscriptions (default off); newsletter and digest production recipients; job times in India time (derived from UTC schedule rules, not observed); bulk worker retries (up to 3, not observed); Acquisition view on production (web signals and attribution default off); contact-request wording for brand-held demands; changes after 2026-11-03.
- Product Q1: should there be an in-panel audit viewer (staff cannot see who changed what)?
- Product Q2: should assigning a high-value lead need the same permission as releasing it?
- Product Q3: should a Contributor be able to see why its bulk rows were rejected (today only in the job history)?
- Product Q4: should operators get a "who is signed in" view (sessions exist but have no screen)?
- Product Q5: should enterprise users receive any WhatsApp or email (today none, by decision)?
- Product Q6: who exactly receives the admin team notifications (all active super admins and admins, a shared address, or a list per event) and can a role or person opt out of an event?
- Product Q7: when do the daily new demands/properties/projects emails go out, should they join the 08:00 newsletter, and should "today" use the India day?
- Product Q8: should notification emails carry phone numbers or a masked number with a link?
- Product Q9: how to handle high-volume bell events; what counts as a "pending sign-up" and which flow approves it (also the Flow 38 table marks the pending sign-up flow as "To confirm").
- Conflict: the Flow 38 table (agent subscribed) body reads "has taken a [Asset class], [City], [Price] subscription for [Total amount]" whereas the Product Documentation 5.3 and persona doc read "a [Asset class] subscription for [City] at [Price], total [Total amount]".
- Conflict: pending sign-up subject is "Pending sign-up — [User type]" in Flow 38 and Product Documentation 5.3, but "Pending sign-up — [User type], [Mobile number]" in the persona doc Section 6.
- Conflict: Flow 38 states the admin-team notification feature is not in code (specification only), while the persona doc describes the notices in Section 6 as live-status unchecked and the Product Documentation 5.3 says build status to be confirmed.
- Conflict: Flow 36 says "View all" includes admin team notifications, while Product Documentation 4.19 says Recent Activity lists only marketing enquiries and listing leads.
- Ambiguity: Flow 2 says "more than 5 codes in 15 minutes" is refused, while the persona doc and Product Documentation say 5 codes in 15 minutes is the cap.
- Ambiguity: Flow 22 uses "eight Tier-1 cities" while the Product Documentation does not list them; the Product Documentation only says "Tier-1 only".
- Ambiguity: Flow 16 step 7 requires "at least one known group" for "Who can see this" but the groups are not listed there (Flow 17 lists developer, Keydemand team, agent).
